chapters.title: Chapter 751: When Wrath Collides
paragraphs: "Oh, I know you've all been eagerly waiting for this moment-the Eternal Challenge!"
Brando, sitting comfortably on his signature talk show sofa, leaned forward with a grin that radiated excitement.
"And with me today," he continued, "is someone who's become a legend in the Kesseon Kingdom-Constantine!"
To his right sat a striking man with shoulder-length blond hair, his presence calm yet commanding.
"Thanks for having me, Brando," Constantine said smoothly. "It's a pleasure to be here."

Brando's smile widened, his energy electric. "Constantine, you've made quite a name for yourself in Kesseon Kingdom-not just as a key figure in the region, but as one of the revered Wrath Champions. But wait, there's more..." He paused dramatically, shifting his hand to point at his left. "Joining us is another Wrath Champion... Booba!"
The man on the other side had dark hair and unmistakable Asian features. He leaned back with an easy grin before flashing a peace sign to the camera.
"Hi, everyone! I'm Booba, the strongest Wrath Champion! Haha!"
"You're definitely brimming with confidence," Brando quipped, shaking his head with a chuckle. "But I can't wait to dive into what we're here for-the Eternal Challenge!"
The studio dimmed slightly as a massive screen behind them lit up, playing the much- anticipated trailer for Immortal Legacy's first grand event.

The screen came to life with the logo of Golden Age Company, followed by the iconic Immortal Legacy emblem. An epic orchestral score began to build as the trailer kicked off with an introduction to the game-its vast landscapes, intricate lore, and the intensity of its battles.

Clips of past moments flashed by: the Deadbay City War, a chaotic clash that left ruins in its wake, followed by the devastating sight of Broken unleashing an earth-shattering arrow from a height, the impact tearing through enemies in the land.

The trailer shifted seamlessly into showcasing highlights from the upcoming Eternal Challenge, teasing the events that would grip the gaming world. The audience was treated to snippets of team battles, solo duels, beast hunts, and even a glimpse of the crafting contest, where players would compete not with weapons, but with skill and ingenuity.

As the trailer reached its climax, the screen faded to black before the date of the event appeared in bold letters. The excitement in the room rose palpably as it became clear-the Eternal Challenge was only days away!
"That's absolutely... spectacular. The anticipation is off the charts," Brando said, turning to face the camera with an electrified smile.

"The excitement, the tension, the rivalries-players from all over the world are already on their way to the competition venue. Tickets have been sold globally, and I know so many fans are eager to finally see their in-game idols in person. The same heroes they've only ever watched on their screens will now be competing live, right in front of a crowd!"
His enthusiasm was infectious, his words carrying the weight of the event's grandeur. "It's going to be an unforgettable moment, and I can't wait to see how it all unfolds!"
Brando smiled, clearly pleased with the energy in the room, before turning to Constantine. "So, what do you think will be the most exciting contest in this competition?"
"Duel of Champions!" Constantine answered without hesitation.

The Duel of Champions was the name given to the solo battle tournament, where the best of the best would face off in an elimination bracket until a single champion emerged victorious in the grand final.
"I knew it!" Brando said, nodding. "Everyone's looking forward to that. What about you, Booba?" He turned to the other Wrath Champion.

"Hah! Of course, the Duel of Champions will be the highlight," Booba replied with a wide grin. "I'll be competing, obviously. But let's be real-my Guild Leader is going to dominate the tournament and take the win. Still, at least I'll make it to the finals to face him." Brando clapped his hands, clearly entertained. "I love the confidence radiating from both of our Wrath Champions tonight. What about you, Constantine? Any thoughts?" Constantine leaned forward slightly, a sharp gleam in his eyes. "You know as well as I do, Booba, that a one-on-one battle like this isn't just about brute strength. It's also about strategy-knowing your opponent's weaknesses and how to exploit them. And frankly, your confidence might be misplaced because I know exactly how your blessing works. You'd struggle even going up against me."

Booba let out a loud laugh, his grin never wavering. "Oh? Is that so? Well then, let me make this more interesting. How about I take you out in the first round, Constantine? That way, I'll clear the path early. What do you think of that?"
Constantine smirked. "Bring it on."
Brando couldn't hide his delight, clapping his hands again. "Now that's the kind of rivalry I like to see! The Duel of Champions is going to be explosive!"

The selection process for the competitors had already been conducted online, with players from around the world competing for their spots. Each team and individual was restricted to participating in no more than two contests, despite the numerous events offered in this grand competition.

The selection process was rigorous, based on in-game tests, overall scores, and the participants' stats and potential. As a result, the competitors arriving now weren't just anyone—they were the best of the best, handpicked for this monumental event.
Several hotels had been carefully selected to accommodate the contestants, each one primed to host the elite participants of the upcoming Eternal Challenge.

A sleek black luxury car pulled up in front of one of the hotels, its polished surface gleaming under the sunlight. Behind the designated line, fans and spectators stood eagerly, their eyes fixed on the scene as they waited for the arrivals.
The car door opened, and a man in his fifties stepped out, his presence immediately drawing gasps from the crowd.
"Goldrich! That's Goldrich!" someone shouted.
"Oh my god, he's so handsome!" another voice gushed.
"Look at him! So rich, so powerful... he's just exuding charisma!"
As Goldrich adjusted his coat and stood with calm authority, another car pulled up behind him. The door opened, and out stepped two figures-a stunning young woman and a sharp-
eyed man.
The crowd erupted again.
"Damn, that's Elincia!"
"Yes, it's Euna—and her brother, Booyoung! He's a Wrath Champion!"
London turned to greet them, waiting patiently as Euna and Booyoung approached. Their entrance added even more weight to the already star-studded arrivals.
"Mr. London, Euna, and Booyoung," one of the spectators whispered excitedly, "I can't wait to see who else from the Vensalor Guild will show up today."
"Wait, isn't Broken supposed to live nearby?" another chimed in.
"Yes, but... I haven't seen him arrive yet," someone replied, scanning the scene with anticipation.
From the hotel entrance, a woman with chestnut brown hair emerged, walking gracefully toward the trio to greet them. It was Freya.
"Hi, welcome to all three of you," she said warmly. "Heejin and Melliandra will be arriving shortly, so let's head inside and gather."
The three nodded and followed her into the hotel lobby.
As they walked, Euna glanced at Freya and asked, "Freya, what about Leon? Is he coming today?"
"Yeah, Freya," Booyoung chimed in. "Where's my brother? Is he joining us or not?"
Freya turned her head, her expression softening into a slightly wry smile. "I'm sure London can help answer that question."
London chuckled quietly as they continued moving, his tone playful as he looked at the two siblings.
"Let's not bother the king too much," he said, giving them a sly wink.

chapters.title: Chapter 752: Glory or Duty
paragraphs: Broken sat quietly in his room, reviewing the items on his backlog. His focus lingered on the upcoming journey to the West Continent. It was a route that was well-traveled, connecting the South and West Continents in a way that made it one of the more straightforward trips. However, the real challenge awaited him once he reached the West Continent. His ultimate goal was a much longer trek-to the location where he suspected he might finally find Ivana.

For now, Aego, the golem ship, would remain under the care of the Vensalor Outriders, ready to support their next journey alongside SexyGrill. Her main quest to locate the floating island was also an immense undertaking that would require time and resources. Both missions were shaping up to be monumental in scope.
Broken leaned back in his chair, his mind turning over the details. What else would he need for this long journey? Another golem? A larger team?

For now, he planned to travel alone. With Goldrich and the others staying behind at the port city as a contingency, it seemed more efficient to go solo for this leg of the trip. Besides, having backup stationed nearby meant he could call on them only if absolutely necessary.

Still, navigating the West Continent brought its own unique challenges. He had the option of working with SexyGrill and her guild, who already had a strong base of operations in the region. Their resources and knowledge of the area could be invaluable.
Well, that settles it, Broken thought to himself. Everything seemed clear now. The plan was in place-he just had to take the first step.
Next, the Eternal Challenge.
Broken paused, his eyes lingering on the entry in his backlog.
The competition was almost here- or more accurately, it was here. In just two days, the first contests would begin, and only now did he realize how much he had overlooked this massive event.

His mind immediately turned to the team contests. The one his team had chosen was Raid Race, a competition where teams raced to conquer a dungeon filled with puzzles, monsters, and a challenging raid boss at the end. It wasn't just about speed but also strategy, teamwork, and efficiency.
Then there was the Team Battle, a tournament where entire teams faced off against each other in a battle of wits, coordination, and raw strength.
Broken exhaled heavily.
Goldrich had repeatedly assured him that he didn't need to stress about the competition. "Leave it to me," Goldrich had said more than once, confidently taking the reins of preparation.
But even so, Broken couldn't shake the feeling that this was something he should be more involved in. After all, it was still his team, his responsibility.
Yet... he couldn't deny the bigger picture.

If he dedicated too much of his attention to the Eternal Challenge, his personal mission-to find Ivana―would be delayed significantly. Time in Yunatea ran three times faster than in the real world, and every hour spent outside the game could mean days lost to his search.
Broken drummed his fingers on the table, contemplating his next move.

With the situation as it was, the only feasible path was to allocate his time wisely. He would participate in the contests he'd committed to, but he couldn't afford to attend the other events or side activities surrounding the competition. They would consume too much of his already limited time.
It was a delicate balancing act, but Broken knew he had no choice but to tread carefully. Ivana's trail wouldn't wait for him.
Next up: the solo contests.

Broken had originally planned to skip this category entirely. There were already too many things on his plate, and solo contests felt like an unnecessary distraction. But thanks to the relentless encouragement from Freya and other guild members, he ended up signing up-not just for one contest, but for two.

Among the available solo contests, there were several that piqued his interest. One, in particular, was the Beast Battle, a tournament where participants would compete by pitting their beasts against each other in thrilling combat.
He couldn't help but picture himself dominating this contest, especially with his extraordinary beast companion, Pawpaw.
But there was a catch.

Due to the tournament-style format, Beast Battle would require a significant time commitment. With the rounds stretching over multiple stages, it was clear that participating in it would interfere with his already tight schedule. After some deliberation, Broken decided to skip the Beast Battle this year.
Maybe next year, he thought, letting the idea go for now.

Instead, he opted for the Blacksmith Crafting Contest, a much more straightforward event. Unlike other contests, this one consisted of a single round-participants would craft their best work, and the winner would be decided immediately.

With this kind of setup, Broken could make good use of his skills while keeping his time free for other priorities. It was a practical choice that allowed him to stay competitive without compromising his overarching mission.
And the final contest...
Broken paused for a moment, then let a faint smile tug at his lips-the Solo Battle
Tournament.

Yes, it was another tournament-style competition, but for some reason, the solo format felt less daunting to him. There was no need to rely on a team or orchestrate complex strategies. It was just him, stepping into the arena, facing whoever stood on the other side.
Besides, Broken had a specific reason for signing up for this one.
He knew Frostedge would also be competing.

The thought of it excited him. This was a rare opportunity to test himself against some of the strongest players in Immortal Legacy. Frostedge wasn't just anyone-he was a legend in his own right. Facing him in battle would be thrilling.
But Frostedge wasn't the only wildcard here.
Would Galactron also participate?
The memory of his last encounter with the prodigy player made Broken exhale sharply.
Even when Broken and Frostedge teamed up against Galactron, the two of them had failed to
defeat him.
No... not exactly failed. Galactron had escaped before they could finish him off, slipping away just when victory seemed within reach.
In the official event, surely Galactron wouldn't be able to do it.

And there was always the looming possibility of another Divine Champion showing up in this competition. With so many powerful players vying for glory, the Solo Battle Tournament promised to be nothing short of extraordinary.
This was shaping up to be a moment of epic proportions, a stage where the strongest clashed. Broken couldn't wait to see how far he could go-and who he would face along the way.

Leon opened his eyes and stepped out of the capsule device. He stretched his stiff muscles, his body craving movement, making him want to sprint or do something to shake off the tension. Just as he was about to act on that thought, Lily appeared at the doorway, her expression
hurried.
"Leon..." she called out.
"Yes?"
"Someone's waiting for you."
"Someone?"
"Yes... don't tell me you forgot you made an appointment with someone. They've been waiting for two hours downstairs in the café."
"An appointment?" Leon frowned, trying to recall. "Who did I make an appointment with?"

Without wasting any more time, he stepped out of the room and headed down to the café in the lounge area. As he entered, his eyes immediately landed on a large man dressed in a casual shirt, seated calmly at one of the tables.
The moment Leon approached, the man stood up, his broad frame making him hard to miss.
"Hi, King," the man said with a grin.
"Hi, too, King," Leon replied, cracking a smile.

chapters.title: Chapter 753: Leon’s new Shield
paragraphs: Leon and King sat across from each other at the small café table. The server arrived with Leon's meal, and he began eating casually as the two of them exchanged a few lighthearted comments.

Their conversation wasn't particularly deep, but it was clear from Leon's relaxed demeanor that he felt comfortable with King. There was an undeniable ease in their dynamic-helped by the fact that King always treated Leon with the utmost respect.
"I've finalized my daughter's school transfer," King said after a pause, his deep voice calm and steady. "And as of today, I'll also be moving here."
Leon couldn't help but smile at that.

In truth, the situation went deeper than what King had just shared. It had started with Leon's growing realization that he might need someone to protect him-someone like a bodyguard or something along those lines.

He sighed inwardly, recalling how things had changed for him. Ever since becoming King Consort, people seemed drawn to him, constantly approaching him either to talk, tease, or simply seek attention. It was exhausting, and while most of it was harmless, it was still a lot to deal with.
It was Freya who had suggested he hire a bodyguard. And though Leon had been hesitant at first, he eventually asked her to help him find the right person.
That's when King, or rather Kingsley, his guildmate from the Vensalor Guild, had stepped up. To Leon's surprise, Kingsley had offered himself for the job without hesitation.
"You really took this offer seriously, huh." Leon said.
King nodded slowly, his expression sincere. "I'd be happy to do something for you."
"You even refused the salary I proposed," Leon replied, leaning back in his chair.
King smiled faintly. "I'll only accept what's fair for me. Besides, I'm not here to be a burden. I'm here to lighten your load."

For someone tasked with being a bodyguard, King was undeniably overqualified. His towering, muscular frame alone was enough to intimidate most people, and his mastery of martial arts made him a formidable force in any physical confrontation. He could drive, handle logistics, and even manage basic tasks with surprising efficiency.

Despite his size and skillset, King's personality was the most striking thing about him. He was gentle and approachable, a man who seemed to radiate kindness. But when he wasn't smiling or speaking, his sheer presence was often enough to make anyone think twice about approaching him.

Even in Immortal Legacy, King-or Kingsley-was known as a tanker beast that no one dared mess with. His reputation was enough to keep trouble at bay, and Leon couldn't help but feel reassured knowing someone like him was now part of his personal life.
Leon extended his hand, and King immediately reached out to shake it firmly.
"Starting today, I officially hire you," Leon said with a small smile.
"Thanks, Broken... Sorry, I mean Leon," King replied.
Leon couldn't help but laugh at the slip.
King smiled and continued, "I'll handle errands for you too if needed. I know Freya's been occupied with a lot of things in the game lately. Besides, I heard you're looking for a new place to stay?"
Leon nodded slowly. "Yes... and I'm still unsure about what kind of place I should go for." "Got any ideas?"

"Freya suggested I buy a building in the city. That way, I could use it for multiple things-like a gym, a café, or even some other spaces-while living on the top floor with my own gaming room and setup."
"You really could afford all of that, huh," King said, raising an eyebrow in amusement.
Leon chuckled at his reaction. "Honestly, I wouldn't know unless I checked my bank balance, but Freya seems pretty confident it's possible."
King leaned back and nodded thoughtfully. "Seriously, buying your own building as a home and workspace sounds pretty awesome. I'll help you find more info about it if you want."

The conversation shifted naturally as they talked about various topics, including their upcoming participation in the Eternal Challenge. King mentioned how some of the guild members had already arrived at the competition venue and were looking for Leon.
"Heejin's already here too," King added. "The first thing she asked about was you."
Leon chuckled, shaking his head. "I'm amazed she's even participating, considering how busy she is as a celebrity."
King grinned. "You didn't know? She's the official singer for the competition's theme song."
"Oh..." Leon blinked, genuinely surprised. "I didn't know that."
"You really don't keep up with things, do you?"

After chatting for a while, Leon changed into his running gear, as did King. They stepped outside for a jog, and this time, for the first time in a long while, Leon wasn't running alone. King, with his massive frame, followed closely behind him.

The sight immediately drew attention from those who were used to seeing Leon jog solo, especially around the park. Many recognized King as Leon's companion from the game, adding an extra layer of intrigue to the scene.
Leon had built a bit of a reputation among the regulars at the park, as he was known for being completely in the zone, oblivious to his surroundings, and running nonstop for over an hour at a time.
"Take your time... I know you need to find Ivana," King said, keeping pace with Leon effortlessly despite his size.
It was remarkable. King, with his towering build, had the stamina and agility to match Leon's tempo, showcasing his strength and flexibility even in real life—not just in the game.
Leon glanced over at him and gave a small nod in response.
"We can handle the battles in the early rounds," King continued, his tone steady. "You don't have to worry about us."
"Thanks," Leon replied simply.
And so, the moment for the Golem Ship Aego to embark on its maiden voyage had finally arrived.
Broken stepped aboard, greeted by the sight of Oriana, the Knights, and Fokil, all gathered to see him off on this significant day. The crew had already taken their positions within the ship.

Though the journey to the West Continent wouldn't take long-the two continents were relatively close-this voyage was crucial. It wasn't just about reaching their destination; it was about testing whether Aego could truly fulfill its purpose.
As the ship began to move, it glided away from the dock with a steady grace. The waters rippled beneath it.

From Mizuki's shoulder, the golem bird suddenly launched into the air, soaring high above. Its mission was clear: to act as their aerial scout, surveying the path ahead and ensuring their safety on this trial journey.

Broken stood at the front of the deck, his eyes fixed on the endless expanse of ocean before him. The salty breeze brushed against his face as he placed a hand on the railing, watching as his dream-the golem ship Aego-finally came to life.
Ronan walked up beside Broken after a few moments of silence, leaning casually on the railing as the two gazed out at the open sea.
"What was the worst monster you've ever encountered out on the ocean, Ronan?"
Ronan's expression shifted as he thought back, then he grinned. "Level 300, Legendary-
grade, King."
Broken turned to him, eyebrows raised. "Legendary-grade monster?" he repeated, his voice tinged with disbelief. "And you survived?"
At that, Ronan burst out laughing, his booming laughter echoing across the deck.
Broken frowned slightly, now even more curious.

chapters.title: Chapter 754: The Serpent's Warning
paragraphs: "Legendary-grade monster?" Broken repeated, still processing Ronan's words.
"Yeah... haha," Ronan replied with a chuckle. "It was both a nightmare and one of the most incredible things we've ever experienced."

He leaned on the railing as he recounted the event. "It was massive... something like a sea serpent or maybe a dragon. I'm not even sure. It just rose out of the ocean, this enormous thing that could've swallowed our entire ship in one bite."
"Just hearing that sounds terrifying," Broken said.
Ronan nodded. "We were lucky, though. The monster didn't actually attack us. I don't know... it felt like it was just warning us. Like it was telling us to turn back and abandon our expedition."

As Ronan spoke, he briefly outlined the journey they'd been on at the time. He and his crew often sought out uncharted waters, challenging themselves to explore areas that no one else in Yunatea had dared venture into.

The world of Yunatea was vast-so vast that even after years of exploration, entire regions of the ocean remained mysterious and untouched. There could be undiscovered islands teeming with hidden creatures, or ancient monsters lurking beneath the waves, waiting for an unsuspecting ship to stumble upon them.

Ronan continued, his tone lighter now. "One time, we found this island where every monster was level 250 or higher. That's part of why our levels are as high as they are now. We've gotten used to fighting some of the strongest monsters out there just to survive."
"That explains a lot," Broken murmured.
"Here, King," Ronan said, pulling out his map. "Let me show you where we ran into that Legendary-grade monster."
He pointed to a specific spot on the map, a seemingly random point far from any known landmass.
Broken leaned in, studying the location. "This... is way out in the middle of nowhere," he said.
"Exactly," Ronan replied. "There's no telling what else is out there. That's what makes it so exciting and so dangerous."

There was something about the location Ronan pointed to on the map that caught Broken's attention. His eyes narrowed as he examined the spot more carefully. It was the exact location SexyGrill had estimated as their next destination for the quest-the place where the Floating Island, the Vensalor Kingdom, was said to be hidden.
Broken froze for a moment, letting the pieces of information click together in his mind. Could there be a connection between the floating island and the Legendary-grade monster Ronan had encountered?
If they were planning to head to that location again, Broken realized, they'd have to be prepared for the possibility of facing that creature head-on.

A Legendary-grade, level 300 monster? It wasn't the first time he and his team had faced something seemingly insurmountable. They'd defeated a Demon above level 400 before, but that victory had been the result of an extraordinary set of circumstances-a collaboration of their best talents and strategies. Ivana in her dragon form. Alora wielding her Golden Paragon. The stars had aligned perfectly, but it wasn't a scenario they could easily replicate. And this time, it wouldn't be on familiar ground.

They'd be fighting in the middle of the ocean-its territory, where the monster held every advantage. Broken grimaced at the thought. On the ship, they'd have limited mobility and resources, forced to rely on Aego to hold its ground against an opponent that could likely crush it without breaking a sweat.
Damn it, he thought.

But despite the daunting odds, Broken couldn't help but feel a surge of excitement coursing through him. This was exactly the kind of high-stakes challenge that stirred his spirit-the kind of mission that made him push beyond his limits.

Later, Broken moved to the lounge area of the ship, enjoying a casual lunch while soaking in the lively atmosphere around him. The crew had started to dance and sing, their laughter and music filling the air, creating a celebratory mood on the deck.

The journey had gone incredibly smoothly-exactly as expected. But what made it even more remarkable was how well Aego performed. The golem ship navigated the ocean with minimal input, requiring only the destination to be set before automatically charting its course. It was a marvel of efficiency, allowing the crew to focus on other tasks without worrying about constant adjustments.

Even so, Ronan and Mizuki diligently monitored their surroundings, ensuring there were no unexpected disturbances. The strait connecting the two continents was considered relatively safe, populated mostly by level-100 monsters. These creatures lived deeper beneath the surface and weren't particularly aggressive unless provoked, making the route one of the calmer stretches of open water.
By late afternoon, the ship began to approach the port city on the West Continent. This was it. For the first time, Broken was about to set foot on another continent.

The West Continent was a land where most of the kingdoms were ruled by Beastkin, even though humans still made up the majority of the population. This unique dynamic became immediately apparent as the ship docked, with nearly half the workers at the harbor being Beastkin.

Broken leaned against the railing, observing the scene with quiet fascination. Beastkin of all kinds, in their half-human forms, bustled about-loading cargo, securing ropes, and directing traffic. Among them were children, their beast-like ears twitching and tails swaying as they ran around, playing without a care in the world.
A faint smile crossed his face as he took in the unique atmosphere.

Once they disembarked, the group began heading toward their designated inn, while some of the crew stayed behind to guard Aego. For this outing, Broken chose to wear his full helmet, concealing his identity entirely.

As they walked through the city, the sights only grew more fascinating. The streets were alive with activity, Beastkin mingling with humans in a way that felt natural but still strikingly different from what Broken was used to.
Even though Beastkin only made up about 30% of the population here, compared to the overwhelmingly human-dominated South Continent, the difference was stark.

The atmosphere in the grand stadium was electric. The stage in the center dominated the view, a colossal structure surrounded by roaring fans. Though the seats weren't yet completely full, the energy from the crowd was palpable as spectators filled the air with their cheers.

The day was perfect-clear skies and a cool breeze-a fitting backdrop for the opening of the Eternal Challenge competition. And to kick things off, the first contest, the Raid Race, was about to begin.

Excitement surged through the arena as a team stepped onto the stage, the name "Destroyer" displayed boldly on the monitors overhead. The crowd erupted into cheers the moment they recognized the players.
"London!"
"Heejin! Oh my god, she's so beautiful in person!"
"That's Melliandra! Damn, she looks exactly like her character in the game."
"King!"
"And... Charmelyn! Wait, what's her real name again? I didn't know she was this gorgeous in real life!"
The noise grew louder, but amidst the excitement, murmurs of confusion began to ripple through the audience.
"Wait... why are there only five of them on stage?"
"Shouldn't there be six?"
"Where's Broken? Isn't he supposed to be part of Team Destroyer?"
"Damn it, where is Broken? They're not seriously going to be beaten in the opening match, are they?"
"They can't! Their opponents this round include two Divine Champions on the same team!"
"Yeah... the strongest team in the US."

chapters.title: Chapter 755: The Opening Raid
paragraphs: Max, a sharp-looking woman with short black hair and glasses, stepped onto the stage with confidence, her mic in hand. The crowd's energy surged as she took center stage, commanding everyone's attention.
"I want to hear your voice!" she shouted.
The stadium erupted with cheers, the audience's excitement reverberating through the massive arena.

"Alright!" Max continued, her voice bright and full of enthusiasm. "I know you've all been waiting for this moment. We have six teams on stage right now, but only two will advance to the next round. Are you ready to see these incredible teams face off in today's Raid Race?"
The crowd roared even louder, their energy almost overwhelming.
Max twirled dramatically, her eyes landing on the massive screen above the stage. "Take a look at the map, everyone!" she said, gesturing to the screen.
The display lit up, revealing a sprawling layout with six separate starting zones branching out into a maze of paths, all converging toward the center.

"This challenge," Max explained, her voice echoing across the stadium, "is all about team performance. Each team must navigate their path, take down monsters, solve puzzles, and finally face the Raid Boss at the end of their route. The winner will be decided by two factors: overall damage dealt and, most importantly, who lands the final hit on the boss!"
The rules were straightforward, but the complexity of the challenge was undeniable. Every team would have to balance speed, strategy, and raw power if they wanted to come out on top.
As Max wrapped up her explanation, the crowd erupted into cheers once more, their anticipation reaching its peak.
Max walked toward a towering man with broad shoulders and short blond hair, her head barely reaching his chest. He stood at the center of one of the teams.
"Alright! This time, we've got Hollow here," Max announced, gesturing toward him. "Also known as one of the Envy Champions! His team is competing under the name ShadowFang!"
The crowd roared as she turned her mic toward Hollow. "So, what do you think, and what are your expectations for this match?"
Hollow's thin smile widened slightly as he glanced toward the camera, his sharp gaze meeting the roaring audience.
"We will come out as the winners," he said confidently.
The crowd erupted in cheers and whistles.
Hollow then turned his attention toward another group on the stage. His smile became a smirk as he spoke again. "We are the strongest team in the US!"
Max leaned in. "Who do you think will be your toughest competitor in this match?"

Hollow scoffed. "No one! There's no one worth mentioning! Or are you talking about the team that's only got five members?" He tilted his head mockingly toward Team Destroyer. "Hah! We will win this easily!"
The audience reacted loudly-some cheering for Hollow's bravado, others buzzing in defense of Team Destroyer.
Max clapped her hands, laughing lightly at his confidence. "Well, we'll see how things play out, Hollow! Let's give it up for Team ShadowFang!"

Max shifted her attention to the figure standing beside Hollow-a striking woman with long blonde hair and glamorous sunglasses, her poised and confident demeanor drawing as much attention as her companion.

"And here we have ScarletDusk!" Max announced, raising her mic toward her. "Everyone knows this team is stacked with not one, but two Divine Champions-Hollow, the Envy Champion, and you, the Lust Champion. So, Scarlet Dusk, what's your take on this opening match?"

Scarlet Dusk offered a dazzling smile before leaning slightly toward the mic. "Actually, I was hoping this would be an exciting match," she said in a smooth, almost teasing tone. "But it doesn't look like that's going to happen. So, yeah... we'll wrap this round up quickly."
Her confidence hit the crowd like a spark, igniting a wave of applause and cheers from the audience.
Max grinned, clearly enjoying the energy Scarlet Dusk brought to the stage. "Well, there you have it, everyone! Let's see if Team ShadowFang can live up to their words!"
The roar of the crowd grew louder, and the anticipation for the match reached new heights as the Divine Champions continued to radiate their unshakable confidence.
While the spotlight was on Team ShadowFang, the members of Team Destroyer exchanged glances, clearly responding to the comments coming from Hollow and ScarletDusk.
"That pair of stupid assholes," Melliandra growled. "I'll shoot holes in both of their heads until they're nothing but Swiss cheese, those two pieces of shit."
Before anyone could react, Max approached Team Destroyer, her mic ready as she turned to Goldrich.
But Melliandra wasn't having it. "Let me talk!" she snapped, cutting in loudly enough to make Max pause.
Max grinned, enjoying the fire. "Oh, we have Melliandra! I know this team has a lot of hardcore fans-let's hear your support!"
The crowd erupted, roaring their approval as Melliandra stepped forward and grabbed the mic from Max's hand without hesitation.
"We're only five people here," she shouted, "but I'm going to shoot every single one of you in the head before we even get to the raid boss! Just watch!"
The stadium exploded in cheers and applause.
Max took the mic back. "That's the kind of fighting spirit we love to see in this competition!"

She then turned to Goldrich, her tone shifting slightly. "Mr. Goldrich, this is such a rare moment, since you almost never appear in public. But I'm sure your fans are dying to hear a few words from you."
Goldrich offered a small smile before stepping forward slightly.
"I have nothing much to say," he began. "But I'll tell you this-don't underestimate us. Five or six, it doesn't matter. We'll show everyone why we're here. Just stay tuned."

As the players began stepping into their designated capsule devices, Max quickly took over the stage again, her voice cutting through the noise of the crowd. Each team had been provided with six capsules, though one would remain unused for Team Destroyer today. Moments after the players settled into their capsules, the large screen above the stage flickered to life. One by one, the avatars of each player materialized on the map displayed for the audience, their names and team banners prominently visible.
The match was about to begin.

Meanwhile, on the other side of the arena, Brando sat in the commentary box, ready to guide the audience through the action. Seated next to him was none other than Paul, the Gluttony Champion, casually dressed in casual style.

"Paul, the first match of this grand competition is about to start," Brando began, his voice animated. "I'd love to hear your thoughts, especially with Team Destroyer missing one of their key members-Broken."

Paul crossed one leg over the other, his expression relaxed as he answered. "The match is designed so that the team that defeats the raid boss first wins. But what's interesting is that, while each team has their own designated track, the map itself is completely open. This means that teams could technically abandon their objectives and engage in an all-out brawl if
they wanted to."

"True," he admitted. "But in a competition like this, with six teams fighting for only two spots in the next round, it's inevitable that the stronger teams will prioritize eliminating the biggest threats first. If one team looks too dangerous, you can bet the others will gang up on them to even the playing field."

Brando nodded thoughtfully. "That's a risky but valid strategy. And with a team like ShadowFang, who are already stacked with two Divine Champions, it might actually be in the other teams' best interest to work together against them. What do you think?"
Paul chuckled lightly. "Perhaps," he said. "But let's not forget, Team Destroyer, even without Broken, is still a powerhouse. If anyone underestimates them, they'll pay the price."

"Simple," Paul said. "Every team is going to abandon their tracks and focus on taking down the Destroyer first. It's the only way the other four teams have a chance to compete for at least second place in this match. As long as the Destroyer stays in the game, they'll dominate." "That's an interesting take," Brando responded as he turned into the camera. "What do you guys think will happen?"

chapters.title: Chapter 756: All Eyes on Team Destroyer
paragraphs: Broken sat in the compact blacksmith workshop area, while the Crawling Carriage Beebot sped across the vast savannah. The golden grass stretched endlessly, swaying gently in the breeze, with only a few scattered trees dotting the landscape.
He had just left Koabia Kingdom, the port city where his journey on the West Continent had begun. His destination was Secobia Kingdom, a region located closer to the center of the continent.

The West Continent, shaped somewhat like an "L," offered two primary routes to reach Secobia. One path followed the left side of the continent, passing through several well- established kingdoms and cities. The other route, on the right side, was a wilderness route- sparsely populated and teeming with untamed monsters.
He had chosen the wilderness.

It wasn't the easiest or safest route, but it was the most discreet. Broken preferred to avoid cities and large settlements whenever possible, especially while traveling alone. The fewer people he encountered, the more focused he could remain on his journey.

Still, he wasn't naive. The wilderness promised more than just solitude-it was crawling with monsters, some of which could pose a significant threat. But for Broken, it was a calculated risk, one he was willing to take.

As Broken settled into his seat, he opened his system interface to pull up a live stream of the Raid Race, the first match of the Eternal Challenge. His eyes locked onto the screen, watching intently as his team-Team Destroyer-stood on the grand stage, surrounded by the roaring cheers of the crowd.
Even while his hands worked on his current task in the mini workshop, his focus occasionally drifted back to the stream. It was strange, seeing them up there without him.

For the past several weeks, Broken had poured every ounce of his attention into his mission- to find Ivana. It felt as if everything else had faded into the background. Sixteen-hour play sessions had become his norm, and the line between his drive and obsession had blurred.
He knew he had no choice but to stay on this path. Ivana's fate was uncertain. Was she safe, or was she being hunted? Was she in need of his help?
Whatever the answer, one thing was clear: Broken had to find her before the High Elf Queen did.

As his team's avatars appeared on the stream and the countdown to the match began, Broken exhaled deeply. He trusted them to handle things in his absence, but the pull to be there, to fight alongside them, lingered.
Yet he couldn't waver now. Not when the stakes were this high.
Brando, serving as the lead caster for the match, spoke with enthusiasm, his voice filled with energy as the audience watched the opening moments of the Raid Race unfold.

"Oh, the match has officially begun! Each team now faces waves of monsters rushing toward them. This is a test of teamwork and strategy-teams must not only survive the waves but also defeat the monsters as quickly as possible. Speed and efficiency are everything here," Brando explained, his commentary sharp and engaging.
On the massive screen, the camera feeds switched between the six teams, each battling fiercely against the relentless waves of monsters.

Paul, seated beside Brando as the match analyst, leaned back and added his thoughts. "You know, there's a reason only two teams can advance to the next round. The final raid boss isn't designed to be defeated by just one team of six players. It's a monster of such immense power that it requires a significant combined force to bring it down. The more teams that survive to the final round, the stronger the overall effort will be."

He paused, smirking slightly. "Of course, before they even get to the boss, they'll probably have to take each other out first. Only two teams can remain standing. That's where things get messy-and interesting."

Brando nodded, a grin spreading across his face as he replied. "That's a strategic gamble, isn't it? Do you focus on pushing through to the raid boss, or do you turn on the other teams to secure your spot in the final two? It's a balancing act, and one wrong move could cost everything."
The screen shifted again, showing Team Destroyer clearing their first wave with swift precision, their coordinated attacks impressing even the commentators.
"Look at that," Brando said, gesturing toward the screen. "Even with just five members, the Destroyer is moving like a well-oiled machine."
"True," Paul agreed. "But let's not forget, every team on this field has their eyes on them. If they're seen as the biggest threat, they could very well become everyone's first target."

The first wave of monsters had finally been defeated. With the field cleared, the teams advanced to the second challenge: a massive gate stood before them, covered in intricate patterns and puzzles that needed to be solved to proceed.
But as the teams approached the gate, the atmosphere shifted dramatically.
"Oh, look at that, Paul!" Brando exclaimed, his voice rising with excitement. "Something you predicted is actually happening!"
The crowd erupted into cheers and shouts as the tension on the screen skyrocketed.
On the live feed, it was clear-two or three players from each team, excluding Team Destroyer, had split off from their groups and were now charging directly toward Destroyer's position.

The melee attackers surged forward, closing the gap with brutal speed, while the long-range attackers aimed their shots from afar. The attacks came fast and without hesitation, an ambush in full force.

"Oh my! Team Destroyer is being swarmed by 12 players at once!" Brando shouted, his voice booming through the stadium. "And look-Hollow and ScarletDusk from ShadowFang are among the attackers! They've joined the fight!"
The screen showed utter chaos as Team Destroyer was suddenly surrounded, arrows, magic, and melee strikes flying in from every direction.

"This is exactly what I expected," Paul said with a smirk. "The other teams see the Destroyer as the greatest threat. By taking them out now, they eliminate their strongest competition and increase their own chances of advancing."
"But can the Destroyer hold their ground with just five players?" Brando questioned.

"It'll come down to how well they can counter this coordinated assault," Paul responded. "Destroyer is skilled, no doubt, but being outnumbered more than two to one, with even Divine Champions like Hollow and Scarlet Dusk in the mix? It's going to be an uphill battle." The audience was on the edge of their seats, watching Team Destroyer's desperate struggle against overwhelming odds. Would they withstand the onslaught, or would this calculated ambush spell their early elimination?
The stadium buzzed with anticipation as the battle unfolded.

The battle intensified, and Brando's voice rose into near hysteria as chaos erupted on the screen. The barrage of long-range attacks raining down on Team Destroyer finally broke through their defenses.

Paul leaned back, a slight smirk tugging at the corner of his lips. "Yes," he said evenly. "This is the end for them. They'll struggle to push back against this coordinated attack. And let's not forget—they're facing opponents like Hollow, who hasn't even activated his Divine Champion Ability yet. The odds are completely stacked against them."
Brando turned to the camera, his excitement practically leaping out of the screen.
"I'm certain the real showdown is about to begin! Will Team Destroyer hold their ground and turn the tide, or will they be the first team to fall in this tournament?"

chapters.title: Chapter 757: The Second Wind of the Destroyer
paragraphs: "Team Destroyer is cornered, being attacked from all directions! They're under constant fire, forced to defend themselves!" Brando continued casting the match with breathless enthusiasm as spells and attacks clashed furiously within the arena.
The tension grew, and the crowd began to rise from their seats, unable to contain their excitement as they watched the intense back-and-forth unfold.
Then, a moment of brilliance emerged.

"Wait-Melliandra! Melliandra is climbing onto Kingsley's back as he shifts into his flying beast form! They're soaring high into the air!" Brando exclaimed, his voice rising with the shift in momentum.

On the massive screen, the audience saw Kingsley take flight, carrying Melliandra high above the battlefield. From this elevated position, their opponents on the ground struggled to respond, the distance and angle making it nearly impossible to land accurate attacks.

Melliandra, now perched safely above the fray, took full advantage of her vantage point. With a wicked grin, she began firing powerful explosive shots, but her targets weren't the attackers currently overwhelming her team. Instead, her blasts rained down on the players who had stayed behind on their respective tracks, focusing on solving the puzzles.

The camera zoomed in on Melliandra's face, capturing her wild laughter as she unleashed devastating explosions from above. With every shot, another player's progress was disrupted, forcing them to abandon their puzzle-solving efforts to dodge the incoming blasts.

"This is incredible!" Brando shouted. "Melliandra's aerial advantage is proving invaluable! The opposing teams didn't account for this at all. From up there, she's landing free hits on their support players and slowing down their progress significantly!"

Paul chimed in with a smirk. "This is the perfect move. By targeting the puzzle solvers, she's forcing the other teams to divide their attention even more. And with no reliable way to counter her from such a height, Team Destroyer just bought themselves some much-needed breathing room."
The audience roared in approval, watching as Melliandra's precise, explosive attacks created chaos across the arena.

Kingsley, now fully transformed into his armored bear form, roared as he charged through the enemy lines, smashing into the attackers with sheer brute force. His massive paws sent players flying, breaking their formation as they tried to regroup.
Meanwhile, Goldrich and Starfall held their ground behind Kingsley, raising protective shields to block incoming attacks while firing precise counterstrikes to keep their enemies at bay.

Then, without warning, a massive dark portal materialized behind Goldrich. The air around it warped ominously, and moments later, a gigantic maw of darkness emerged, firing a devastating cannon-like blast that tore through the enemy ranks. The force of the attack forced the opposing players to retreat, scrambling to recover and regroup.
Among the retreating attackers, Hollow, the Envy Champion, stood his ground. A sudden magic circle appeared beside him.
The audience gasped audibly as the summoning began.
From the circle emerged a massive giant monster, wielding an enormous stone club, its size nearly matching that of Kingsley's bear form. The tension in the stadium spiked as the creature roared.
"That's it!" Paul exclaimed, his voice cutting through the rising cheers of the crowd. "That's Hollow's Divine Champion ability!
Brando, wide-eyed, leaned toward Paul. "Paul, tell us what do we know about Hollow and his Envy Champion Blessing?"

Paul nodded, his voice steady as he explained. "Envy Champions are known for their avatar- based abilities. Some can duplicate themselves, while others, like Hollow, can duplicate creatures they've defeated in battle. That's what makes him so dangerous. This giant? It's a high-grade monster, possibly with a high level, and it's something Hollow likely defeated in the past, giving him the ability to summon it at will."
Brando's excitement grew. "That's incredible! Are you saying that if Hollow defeated a Named Demon or other high-level entities, he could summon them too?"

Paul smirked. "It's entirely possible. Though he missed his chance to do that during the war in Dissidia. If Hollow had taken down even one Named Demon, it would've been a game- changing ability for him."

On the screen, the battle escalated. The giant monster, wielding its massive stone club, charged at Kingsley in his bear form. The two collided with thunderous force, the ground shaking beneath them. The giant's club came crashing down, hitting Kingsley squarely, sending him staggering backward. The bear let out a pained roar as the force of the blow sent him tumbling to the ground with a heavy thud.
The crowd erupted into cheers and gasps, the tension skyrocketing as the balance of power shifted again.
"But, Paul," Brando pressed, his excitement building, "doesn't a summoner like Hollow have a significant weakness if they're taken out directly?"

Paul nodded thoughtfully. "Yes, that's true for most summoners. But let's not forget- Hollow isn't purely a summoner. He's a fighter, and more specifically, a close-range combatant. That's what makes him so unique as an Envy Champion."
Brando leaned in, his curiosity evident. "But do you think Hollow can break through the Destroyer's defenses? Especially with Goldrich and Starfall standing in his way?"

Paul smirked, pointing toward the screen. "That's exactly where their advantage lies. Remember, ShadowFang has two Divine Champions-not just Hollow, but also ScarletDusk. And that changes everything."

The action on the screen intensified as Hollow shot forward with astonishing speed, closing the distance to Goldrich in mere moments. His movements were almost impossible to track, and his fists slammed relentlessly into the protective shield conjured by Goldrich, the force shaking the ground beneath them.

Starfall, positioned carefully, launched an array of crowd-control abilities at Hollow—magic binds, slowing fields, and even precise strikes. But it was clear that none of it was enough to hold Hollow back.

Hollow's lips curled into a faint smirk as he broke through the layers of defense, moving within striking range of Goldrich. But Goldrich smirked right back. Suddenly, a massive explosion erupted from Goldrich's body, forcing Hollow backward. The crowd gasped in unison.
Onlookers held their breath, wondering if the blast had taken Hollow out.
But as the dust cleared, Hollow emerged unscathed, his speed allowing him to reposition almost instantly. He charged forward once more, his relentless attacks focused entirely on
Goldrich.

Meanwhile, in the VIP section, Maylon sat beside Euna, casually watching the chaos unfold on the battlefield. Lily was seated nearby, next to Maylon's young daughter, who watched the screen with wide eyes.
"The key isn't Hollow," Maylon said.
"Is it ScarletDusk?" Euna asked, raising an eyebrow.
"Exactly. Her abilities as the Lust Champion are what make this combination dangerous."
Euna tilted her head. "What do you know about her Blessings?"

"I suspect her ability allows her to lend stats or skills to Hollow from a distance. Similar to how SexyGrill's ability boosts the levels of players bonded to her. Scarlet Dusk is essentially empowering Hollow, making him exponentially stronger than he would be on his own." Euna's expression grew serious. "So the real strategy for Team Destroyer should be to find Scarlet Dusk and take her out before Hollow overpowers Starfall and breaks through their defensive line. If she's hidden somewhere and continues boosting him, the Destroyer won't be able to hold him back for long."

Maylon nodded with a faint smile. "Exactly. Hollow is strong, but without ScarletDusk supporting him, he won't be able to overwhelm Destroyer's defenses. The clock is ticking- they'll need to figure this out before it's too late."
[Daniel_Daye_4365]: "Melliandra really said she'd shoot everyone in the head, and she's doing it like a psycho from the sky."
[EvilNCarnate]: "Imagine sweating over a puzzle, trying to figure out a pattern, and BOOM, Melliandra says, 'Nah, not today.' I'd uninstall the game."

got yeeted across the field and still stood up like a champ."

and it's like she's painting on a canvas."

Destroyer.

The tension rose as the camera shifted to another area, revealing Charmelyn appearing in two places at once. In the blink of an eye, she duplicated herself into numerous copies, launching an all-out attack on the opposing team, who were already struggling to defend themselves from Melliandra's relentless aerial assault.
"This fight isn't over yet! Team Destroyer is putting up a fierce resistance!" Brando shouted at the top of his lungs, his voice echoing across the arena.

sentences.text: "Team Destroyer is cornered, being attacked from all directions!
They're under constant fire, forced to defend themselves!" Brando continued casting the match with breathless enthusiasm as spells and attacks clashed furiously within the arena.
The tension grew, and the crowd began to rise from their seats, unable to contain their excitement as they watched the intense back-and-forth unfold.
Then, a moment of brilliance emerged.
"Wait-Melliandra!
Melliandra is climbing onto Kingsley's back as he shifts into his flying beast form!
They're soaring high into the air!" Brando exclaimed, his voice rising with the shift in momentum.
On the massive screen, the audience saw Kingsley take flight, carrying Melliandra high above the battlefield.
From this elevated position, their opponents on the ground struggled to respond, the distance and angle making it nearly impossible to land accurate attacks.
Melliandra, now perched safely above the fray, took full advantage of her vantage point.
With a wicked grin, she began firing powerful explosive shots, but her targets weren't the attackers currently overwhelming her team.
Instead, her blasts rained down on the players who had stayed behind on their respective tracks, focusing on solving the puzzles.
The camera zoomed in on Melliandra's face, capturing her wild laughter as she unleashed devastating explosions from above.
With every shot, another player's progress was disrupted, forcing them to abandon their puzzle-solving efforts to dodge the incoming blasts.
"This is incredible!" Brando shouted.
"Melliandra's aerial advantage is proving invaluable!
The opposing teams didn't account for this at all.
From up there, she's landing free hits on their support players and slowing down their progress significantly!"
Paul chimed in with a smirk.
"This is the perfect move.
By targeting the puzzle solvers, she's forcing the other teams to divide their attention even more.
And with no reliable way to counter her from such a height, Team Destroyer just bought themselves some much-needed breathing room."
The audience roared in approval, watching as Melliandra's precise, explosive attacks created chaos across the arena.
Kingsley, now fully transformed into his armored bear form, roared as he charged through the enemy lines, smashing into the attackers with sheer brute force.
His massive paws sent players flying, breaking their formation as they tried to regroup.
Meanwhile, Goldrich and Starfall held their ground behind Kingsley, raising protective shields to block incoming attacks while firing precise counterstrikes to keep their enemies at bay.
Then, without warning, a massive dark portal materialized behind Goldrich.
The air around it warped ominously, and moments later, a gigantic maw of darkness emerged, firing a devastating cannon-like blast that tore through the enemy ranks.
The force of the attack forced the opposing players to retreat, scrambling to recover and regroup.
Among the retreating attackers, Hollow, the Envy Champion, stood his ground.
A sudden magic circle appeared beside him.
The audience gasped audibly as the summoning began.
From the circle emerged a massive giant monster, wielding an enormous stone club, its size nearly matching that of Kingsley's bear form.
The tension in the stadium spiked as the creature roared.
"That's it!" Paul exclaimed, his voice cutting through the rising cheers of the crowd.
"That's Hollow's Divine Champion ability!
Brando, wide-eyed, leaned toward Paul.
"Paul, tell us what do we know about Hollow and his Envy Champion Blessing?"
Paul nodded, his voice steady as he explained.
"Envy Champions are known for their avatar- based abilities.
Some can duplicate themselves, while others, like Hollow, can duplicate creatures they've defeated in battle.
That's what makes him so dangerous.
This giant?
It's a high-grade monster, possibly with a high level, and it's something Hollow likely defeated in the past, giving him the ability to summon it at will."
Brando's excitement grew.
"That's incredible!
Are you saying that if Hollow defeated a Named Demon or other high-level entities, he could summon them too?"
Paul smirked.
"It's entirely possible.
Though he missed his chance to do that during the war in Dissidia.
If Hollow had taken down even one Named Demon, it would've been a game- changing ability for him."
On the screen, the battle escalated.
The giant monster, wielding its massive stone club, charged at Kingsley in his bear form.
The two collided with thunderous force, the ground shaking beneath them.
The giant's club came crashing down, hitting Kingsley squarely, sending him staggering backward.
The bear let out a pained roar as the force of the blow sent him tumbling to the ground with a heavy thud.
The crowd erupted into cheers and gasps, the tension skyrocketing as the balance of power shifted again.
"But, Paul," Brando pressed, his excitement building, "doesn't a summoner like Hollow have a significant weakness if they're taken out directly?"
Paul nodded thoughtfully.
"Yes, that's true for most summoners.
But let's not forget- Hollow isn't purely a summoner.
He's a fighter, and more specifically, a close-range combatant.
That's what makes him so unique as an Envy Champion."
Brando leaned in, his curiosity evident.
"But do you think Hollow can break through the Destroyer's defenses?
Especially with Goldrich and Starfall standing in his way?"
Paul smirked, pointing toward the screen.
"That's exactly where their advantage lies.
Remember, ShadowFang has two Divine Champions-not just Hollow, but also ScarletDusk.
And that changes everything."
The action on the screen intensified as Hollow shot forward with astonishing speed, closing the distance to Goldrich in mere moments.
His movements were almost impossible to track, and his fists slammed relentlessly into the protective shield conjured by Goldrich, the force shaking the ground beneath them.
Starfall, positioned carefully, launched an array of crowd-control abilities at Hollow—magic binds, slowing fields, and even precise strikes.
But it was clear that none of it was enough to hold Hollow back.
Hollow's lips curled into a faint smirk as he broke through the layers of defense, moving within striking range of Goldrich.
But Goldrich smirked right back.
Suddenly, a massive explosion erupted from Goldrich's body, forcing Hollow backward.
The crowd gasped in unison.
Onlookers held their breath, wondering if the blast had taken Hollow out.
But as the dust cleared, Hollow emerged unscathed, his speed allowing him to reposition almost instantly.
He charged forward once more, his relentless attacks focused entirely on
Goldrich.
Meanwhile, in the VIP section, Maylon sat beside Euna, casually watching the chaos unfold on the battlefield.
Lily was seated nearby, next to Maylon's young daughter, who watched the screen with wide eyes.
"The key isn't Hollow," Maylon said.
"Is it ScarletDusk?" Euna asked, raising an eyebrow.
"Exactly.
Her abilities as the Lust Champion are what make this combination dangerous."
Euna tilted her head.
"What do you know about her Blessings?"
"I suspect her ability allows her to lend stats or skills to Hollow from a distance.
Similar to how SexyGrill's ability boosts the levels of players bonded to her.
Scarlet Dusk is essentially empowering Hollow, making him exponentially stronger than he would be on his own." Euna's expression grew serious.
"So the real strategy for Team Destroyer should be to find Scarlet Dusk and take her out before Hollow overpowers Starfall and breaks through their defensive line.
If she's hidden somewhere and continues boosting him, the Destroyer won't be able to hold him back for long."
Maylon nodded with a faint smile.
"Exactly.
Hollow is strong, but without ScarletDusk supporting him, he won't be able to overwhelm Destroyer's defenses.
The clock is ticking- they'll need to figure this out before it's too late."

chapters.title: Chapter 758 - From Boss to Punching Bag
paragraphs: On the giant screen, the focus shifted to Charmelyn as she unleashed a flurry of attacks on the opposing team with lightning-fast movements, accompanied by her seemingly endless duplicates.

Just as her opponents managed to mount a defense, she would vanish without a trace, only to reappear in another part of the arena, catching another team off guard. Her sudden attacks left her enemies reeling, completely unprepared for the chaos she brought.

Even though the opposing players were all above level 200, Charmelyn's ability to disappear and reappear unpredictably—combined with her clones' relentless distractions—allowed her to take out the enemy team's support player with precision.

Meanwhile, Melliandra darted across floating platforms in the air, creating havoc that left the opponents torn between defending against aerial assaults or ground-level attacks. The confusion proved fatal when Charmelyn closed in on a group working on a puzzle and brutally eliminated all three players. Their names and profiles on the screen instantly turned red, signaling their elimination from the match.
The crowd erupted in cheers as they witnessed the merciless rampage led by Charmelyn and Melliandra.
"Charmelyn and Melliandra are delivering an incredible performance! Their combination is absolutely deadly. But the real question is—how is Charmelyn teleporting around the arena?" Brando exclaimed.
Paul smirked and leaned back casually. "There hasn't been an official statement from the Vensalor Guild, but my guess? Charmelyn is the new Divine Champion—the Envy Champion."
"Oh, so the rumors about the Divine Champion powers being transferable are true? Does this mean Charmelyn managed to claim it for herself?" Brando asked, eyes wide with curiosity.
Paul gave a knowing smile and raised his hands. "I'm not in a position to confirm anything. Let the people decide for themselves."
"This is absolutely fascinating! This battle is nothing like we expected. Are we witnessing the rise of another Divine Champion in this arena?!" Brando's voice rose above the roaring crowd.
[Syrestage]: "Those poor puzzle guys were just trying to mind their own business and solve Sudoku or something, then BOOM—Charmelyn said 'No puzzles today, only pain.'"
[WhitakerD]: "As a support main, watching this hurts. Charmelyn took 'kill the healer first' and turned it into a whole personality."
[David_Howe_1003]: "Can we get a moment of silence for that team? Actually, never mind—Charmelyn already gave them eternal silence."
[Carl_Chalmers]: "The real puzzle was figuring out how to survive for more than 30 seconds. Spoiler: they didn't."
[Michael_Mason_4134]: "Team Destroyer? More like Team Destroy-everything-you-love. This is a massacre, not a match."
[Drop_BearX]: "Charmelyn and Melliandra aren't playing to win; they're playing to make sure their enemies need therapy after this.
[Mason_Rogers_7744]: "Honestly, if I were on that team, I'd just logout and go make a sandwich. No point fighting when you're already in a highlight reel."

While it was clear that Hollow and the other attackers were still holding their ground against Goldrich and his allies, Charmelyn relentlessly continued her assault. Now, she had even infiltrated Team ShadowFang, wreaking havoc as she attempted to take them down one by one.
From the frontline, Hollow appeared to be losing his patience as he witnessed this chaos unfold, launching an even more ferocious attack in frustration.
However, the tide of the battle shifted dramatically when ScarletDusk was suddenly exposed from her invisibility state, only to be met with a merciless onslaught from both Melliandra and Charmelyn.
Despite her teammates' best efforts, they couldn't save ScarletDusk. In the end, the Lust Champion was obliterated, her presence erased from the arena entirely.
The audience collectively gasped, stunned by the sheer brutality of what they had just witnessed—executed by only two players.

With ScarletDusk's defeat, Hollow suddenly found himself at a severe disadvantage. His once-aggressive offense faltered, and he quickly transitioned into a defensive stance, his movements no longer carrying the same ferocity as before.
"ScarletDusk has been taken down!" Brando shouted. "And now, Hollow is losing momentum and shifting to a defensive mode!"
"I think this might be the end for Hollow too," Paul remarked calmly.
Right on cue, the giant monster that had been dominating the battlefield disappeared, followed closely by the Envy Champion, Hollow himself.
The arena erupted into deafening cheers as the crowd celebrated the thrilling conclusion of the fight.

"But, Paul," Brando pressed, his tone shifting to one of curiosity, "if Team Destroyer keeps up this rampage, do you think they'll actually be able to defeat the Raid Boss at the end? Because if they can't take it down, this match will still end without a single winner."
"Well," Paul said with a slight smirk, "let's hope they have a plan for that."
[Epsilon13]: "The way Team Destroyer is playing, I wouldn't be surprised if the Raid Boss just logs off out of fear."
[Tsniper]: "The other teams are playing a game. Team Destroyer is writing obituaries."
[Eye_of_Wolf]: "At this point, it's not Team Destroyer; it's Team Disrespect.
[Nuke4757]: "Hollow watching his entire team get wiped out like: 'I didn't sign up for this.'"
[Tim_Holman]: "Team Destroyer out here speedrunning the elimination of players like they forgot there's still a whole Raid Boss waiting to clap them."
The match continued as Team Destroyer advanced through the game, successfully solving the puzzle and moving on to face the Raid Boss.

Meanwhile, the remaining teams? They were reduced to mere remnants, with only a handful of players left from the four original groups. Team Destroyer had already annihilated ShadowFang, leaving no chance for recovery.

But in a surprising twist, Kingsley, the team's tank, took on the Raid Boss head-on, holding its attacks singlehandedly while the rest of the team unleashed a relentless barrage of damage. The Raid Boss, which should have been a formidable challenge, was reduced to nothing more than a punching bag for Team Destroyer.

Even with just five members, the Raid Boss failed to mount any significant resistance against them. As for the remnants of the other teams who had finally completed the puzzle? They didn't dare to approach, too terrified of suffering the same fate as ShadowFang at the hands of Team Destroyer.

In the end, Team Destroyer triumphed. They defeated the Raid Boss in spectacular fashion, and their team name lit up the arena in a burst of colorful confetti, announcing them as the victors of the match.

The crowd was stunned into silence for a moment before Brando's voice cut through the air, roaring with excitement to celebrate their win. His energy ignited the audience, who quickly joined in with deafening cheers.

The second-place finishers were one of the few surviving teams who had dealt only minimal damage to the Raid Boss, clearly more focused on staying alive than taking risks. But all eyes remained on Team Destroyer, whose dominance had left an unforgettable mark on the arena.
Maylon and Euna, seated among the spectators, continued their discussion as the match wrapped up.

Maylon sighed and said, "They should've known by now that Melliandra has that kind of attack range. They didn't even try to counter her. On top of that, she's got massive physical damage that can ignore defense entirely."
"I think the opponents underestimated them because they're only five players," Euna replied thoughtfully.

"That's probably it," Maylon agreed, nodding. "What they didn't account for is that the current Vensalor Guild members almost all have at least Unique-grade weapons. They completely overlooked the significance of that. Even though Broken didn't show up in person, he was definitely present through his crafted weapons."
Euna chuckled softly. "If Broken had actually shown up, the match would've been over in half the time, don't you think?"
