chapters.title: Chapter 776: Fast and Deadly
paragraphs: Leon stepped onto the stage, greeted by the roaring cheers of the audience. It was clear—today's crowd was even larger than the day before.
And yet, they all knew the match would likely end in seconds.
Then again, it made sense.

Each batch of matches featured multiple fights in rotation, and as the tournament progressed, more top-tier players were stepping into the arena. Naturally, that drew in even more fans eager to watch their favorites compete.
At the opposite end of the stage, his opponent ascended as well.
The host, as energetic as ever, took center stage and immediately hyped up the moment, his voice booming across the arena.
And just like that, the brief pre-match interview began.
Leon's least favorite part of the event.
Because, at this stage, every answer players gave fell into one of two categories—either they sounded overconfident, or they downplayed their opponent.
Was there really no other way to respond?

Well, at the very least, this was one of the few moments where Leon could afford to act a little arrogant—without actually looking too arrogant. Because, after all, everyone else was doing the same thing.
Stormbreaker was the first to respond when the host handed him the mic.
"I'm confident this will be an easy win. No doubt about it." His voice was steady, almost dismissive. "No need to talk—let's just settle this in the game."
He smirked slightly before continuing.
"Will my opponent rely on massive AOE magic? A strong single-target skill? Or maybe refined melee techniques?" He let the question hang for a moment. "Doesn't matter. I can handle them all."
The crowd erupted in cheers, fueling the already intense energy in the stadium.
And this... was exactly what Freya had warned Leon about earlier.
His opponent this time wasn't someone he could take lightly.
From what he had gathered, Stormbreaker's blessing was, he had a 100% critical hit rate. Which meant every attack he landed was guaranteed to be lethal.
A true Pride Champion blessing—completely overpowered.
On top of that, his class made him a nightmare to deal with. It was heavily influenced by the Shadow Element, granting him not only devastating attack power but also exceptional evasive abilities.
That was what made him so dangerous—he wasn't just about brute force, but also hard to hit.
Even worse?
According to Freya, Stormbreaker had a solution for every type of combat—whether it was melee or ranged.
Which meant Leon couldn't just fly into the air and bombard him with arrows like he usually did.
Stormbreaker was prepared for that too.
Leon took the mic and responded calmly.
"This will be a valuable experience for me. I just hope I don't lose too quickly."
The host chuckled.
"Oh wow, that's a surprisingly humble response from Broken!"
With the pre-match interviews over, both Leon and Stormbreaker stepped toward their capsule devices.
As they prepared to enter, the betting odds flashed across the big screen—47 to 53 in favor of Stormbreaker.
It wasn't surprising. Stormbreaker's popularity was overwhelming.
Compared to him, Broken was still a rising name—someone who had only recently gained attention.
Meanwhile, players like Stormbreaker had already built their reputation over time, making him the clearer favorite in the eyes of the audience.
Over at the casters' desk, Brando was joined by Paul, both ready to break down the upcoming match between two of the most talked-about players in the tournament.

"Paul, this is going to be really exciting," Brando began, his enthusiasm evident. "We all know that Stormbreaker is no ordinary player. He has devastating attacks, his technique is top-tier, and his class makes him a nearly unstoppable fighter. Some even say he can go toe-to-toe with Frostedge in a one-on-one battle."
He then shifted gears.

"On the other hand, we have Broken—a player with an insane amount of force behind him. His summons, his versatility, and his overpowered skills make him a force to be reckoned with. So, who do you think has the upper hand?"
Paul took a moment to consider the question before responding.

"Well, I want to say Broken has a shot at winning here. But if we really break it down, his abilities are better suited for large-scale battles where he can take on multiple enemies at once. And in terms of close combat? That's a major advantage for Stormbreaker, who specializes in melee combat."
Brando nodded but countered, "But what about Broken's bow? Can't he just fight safely from the air? And let's not forget—he has the Golden Paragon."
Paul leaned forward, his expression thoughtful.
"We know that Stormbreaker has an ability that allows him to control wind, which lets him soar to higher altitudes. So unless Broken can outrun him in the air, he won't be safe."

He then added, "As for the Golden Paragon... we still don't fully understand how that skill works, but I'd bet it has a limited activation time. If Stormbreaker can survive long enough for Broken to burn through his strongest skills, he'll have a perfect opening to strike back and secure the win."
"That's an interesting analysis. I'm sure everyone is eager to see how this unfolds," Brando responded.
At that moment, the crowd's attention shifted to the big screen, where the two players were now standing face-to-face, ready for battle.
The countdown ticked down toward zero, and Broken immediately prepared himself.
He equipped his upgraded version of Invincible Paragon and drew his spear, ready to test just how strong his opponent was before deciding on a proper strategy to counter him.
He couldn't afford to recklessly use Golden Paragon.
That avatar had strict limitations, and if Broken couldn't maintain it long enough to defeat his opponent before it expired, he would be left at a major disadvantage.
On top of that, Golden Paragon came with a 48-hour cooldown—which meant using it without careful planning could cost him future matches in the tournament.
With more battles ahead, he needed to be strategic.
Broken steadied himself as Stormbreaker confidently gripped his sword.
A dark aura wrapped around Stormbreaker's body, a clear sign that he had activated his Shadow Element abilities.
A melee fighter with shadow-based skills and insane speed.
No—this was worse.
He fought like an assassin, but even deadlier. Because every single attack he landed was a 100% critical hit.
If this guy's sword had low crit rate but high base damage, then this was going to be a nightmare to deal with.
Stormbreaker rushed forward, his movement sharp and precise, closing the distance in an instant.
Broken tightened his grip on his spear, already having activated all his protective skills.
Time to test just how deadly this guy really was. Hopefully, he wouldn't be disappointed—a proper fight like this would actually be fun for once.
The moment Stormbreaker reached him, he swung his sword in a clean, calculated arc.
Broken reacted swiftly, blocking with his spear.
[Spear Guard (Conditional Passive Skill) Lv. 6 Activated]
Immediately, Stormbreaker was knocked backward, thrown off by his own attack.
Not bad.
But within a split second, he recovered.
Then, he vanished—no, not vanished. He moved too fast for the eye to follow.
Before Broken could fully track him, Stormbreaker circled around and launched a blindingly fast slash from behind.
Damn!
Broken felt it.
This guy was fast and deadly.

chapters.title: Chapter 777: Luck Runs Out
paragraphs: Broken was deliberately testing his opponent's strength, focusing on defense while looking for opportunities to counterattack whenever possible.
But it was becoming painfully clear—Stormbreaker was no ordinary swordsman. His speed was unreal. His attack rate was relentless.
Even though Broken was playing defensively, blocking and absorbing the incoming strikes, Stormbreaker still managed to land countless consecutive attacks.

Fortunately, Broken had layers of protective skills, nullifying a good portion of the damage while his high health and recovery rate kept him standing. At the same time, this also meant Stormbreaker couldn't finish him off easily.

Still, the situation was getting frustrating. Every time Broken tried to move, to create space for a counterattack, Stormbreaker immediately closed the gap, his speed outpacing every attempt to escape. This was starting to get annoying.
"You've got a solid defense for a mere spear fighter, huh?" Stormbreaker taunted.
Broken smirked, still blocking his opponent's relentless onslaught.
"Thanks for the compliment. I feel honored."
Stormbreaker scoffed.
"No amount of defense can withstand my blade. My Divine Champion blessing ensures that no one escapes my sword alive!"
And yes—Broken had to admit. This guy was impressive. Not only did he have an overpowered blessing, but his swordplay was genuinely exceptional.
The only other time Broken had felt this level of technical skill in a fight was when he had faced Frostedge.
But there was one major difference.
Frostedge's attack speed had been something Broken could still keep up with. But Stormbreaker? His speed was on another level entirely.
"Now, summon all your creatures—" Stormbreaker taunted, his blade flashing as he continued his relentless assault. "Isn't that what you usually do? Hiding behind your summons?"
He struck fast, his sword slicing through the air, but the moment Broken counterattacked, Stormbreaker instantly retreated, avoiding the blow with flawless movement.
He dodged everything.
Single-target attacks? Easily avoided. Wide-area attacks? Effortlessly sidestepped.
Every time Broken aimed his spear, Stormbreaker would redirect it, deflecting the attack before it could land.
And then, before Broken could adjust, the man would sink into the shadows—only to reappear somewhere else, launching another attack.
He wasn't just fighting like an assassin—he was far worse. A high-damage, critical-hit-abusing nightmare with insane mobility.
So fucking lucky.
But why wasn't Broken using his summons?
Sure, they would have made things easier. He had summons capable of ranged attacks, which could help him create openings while keeping his opponent distracted.
If he summoned Gaia, he could turn the tide of battle significantly in his favor.
But no—he had a reason for holding back.
For one, Stormbreaker's evasive skills were ridiculous. He could slip into the shadows and reappear anywhere, making it difficult for any summon to keep up with him.
More importantly, his attacks were lethal. If he managed to land direct hits, he could wipe out Broken's summons instantly.
But beyond that...
There was something else Broken had been planning.
He just needed to confirm a few more things—he wanted Stormbreaker to fully reveal his combat style and abilities in a one-on-one setting first.
And now, he had seen enough.
A slow smirk formed on his lips. It was time to make Stormbreaker regret ever facing him in the Duel of Champions.
The audience watching the match began buzzing with commentary as the fight continued.
From an outsider's perspective, it seemed like Broken was only defending, while Stormbreaker relentlessly attacked without stopping.
To anyone watching, the battle looked completely one-sided—the winner seemingly obvious just by observation.
"Hah, I feel bad for anyone who bet on Broken. Another easy win for me."
"Damn it, why is Broken just defending? Why isn't he using his bow? Doesn't he have high-damage attacks?"
"Didn't you hear? Stormbreaker can just chase him into the air and attack while Broken takes forever to charge his skill."
"Man, this fight is so one-sided. I don't see how Broken can win this."
"Broken still has his Golden Paragon. If he uses that, he'll definitely win."
"Stormbreaker just needs to stall and wait for the skill to expire, hah!"
Suddenly, the big screen showed a shift in the battle.
Stormbreaker, who had been attacking relentlessly, suddenly retreated after his last strike. For the first time, he paused, no longer attacking as aggressively as before.
What just happened?!
That was when the audience noticed it.

Broken was no longer holding his spear. Instead, in his hands was a massive greatsword—far heavier and broader than his previous weapon. Its shape resembled a cracked, fragile gravestone, its surface covered in deep fractures, as if it could shatter at any moment.
Had Broken changed his strategy?!
Over at the casters' desk, Brando immediately spoke up.
"Oh? Broken just switched to a greatsword! That's an interesting choice."
He leaned forward, intrigued.

"Greatswords are great for parrying, sure—but they come with a huge drawback. Broken is sacrificing attack speed, which means he'll have an even harder time keeping up with Stormbreaker's relentless attacks."
Paul analyzed the situation carefully before adding his own thoughts.
"I think there's a special effect on that greatsword."
His gaze flicked to Stormbreaker, who was still keeping his distance.
"Something happened after that last exchange. Stormbreaker backed off after his attack was parried, and he hasn't immediately resumed his assault.
He narrowed his eyes.
"Whatever that sword does, Broken must have chosen it for a reason."
From Broken's perspective, he stood firm, holding his Gravestone Greatsword in a parry stance, fully prepared to counter any incoming attacks.
And if Stormbreaker recklessly continued his assault? There was a real possibility his sword would break completely.

The Eternal Challenge tournament was held on a private server, separate from Immortal Legacy's main game. However, there was a crucial rule—whatever happened during the tournament would remain in effect until it was over.
That meant if a piece of equipment was destroyed during a match, it would stay broken for the rest of the competition.
If Stormbreaker lost his sword here, he would be at a huge disadvantage for the remaining rounds.
And considering how long the Eternal Challenge still had to go, that kind of loss would be devastating for him.
Stormbreaker seemed to realize this. His sword's durability had dropped significantly from their last clash.
And honestly? Broken respected that.
At least Stormbreaker had enough awareness to notice the risk—unlike SpeedGang, that brainless idiot who kept attacking until he completely shattered his weapon.
"You're such a cheater!" Stormbreaker snapped, frustration in his voice.
"Oh?" Broken smirked. "Says the guy with a 100% critical rate."
There was one more disadvantage now pushing Stormbreaker into a corner—
His own blessing.
And Broken found it absolutely hilarious. Because every time Stormbreaker's sword landed a critical hit, its durability dropped even faster.
So, in the most ironic twist possible, the very blessing that had made him seem unstoppable had now become his greatest curse.
His super 777 kind of luck had run out— And he was about to be destroyed by the very blessing everyone once called cheating. If he kept attacking, he would lose his weapon.
Now, the question was—
What would this so-called Pride Champion do?
"I'll finish you off before anything happens to my sword," Stormbreaker declared.
Broken smirked. "You really trust your luck that much, huh?"
"This isn't luck. This is fate."
Stormbreaker's stance tightened, his focus sharpening.
He was ready to attack again.
So now, the real question—
Would luck win?
Or would Broken's overpowered greatsword hold its ground?

chapters.title: Chapter 778 - The Dormant Fae Seed
paragraphs: Okay, the second round begins!
Broken immediately recast every protective skill he had, preparing to withstand Stormbreaker's relentless speed.
As expected, Stormbreaker launched another furious assault, his sword slashing through the air like a blur.
But just as before—Broken parried one of the attacks. A massive spark erupted upon impact. A guaranteed critical hit. Which meant Stormbreaker's weapon durability had dropped even further.
Out of three or four attacks, Broken only managed to parry one, while the rest landed cleanly on him.
But...
He was still standing.
Thanks to Invincible Paragon, his armor had multiple layers of defensive skills, allowing him to endure the hits while continuously cycling his defensive buffs.
And as the battle continued—
Broken started adapting.
The more Stormbreaker attacked, the more Broken read his movements. And the more Broken read his movements, the more parries he successfully landed.
Each successful parry chipped away at Stormbreaker's sword durability—
And every time it happened, Broken smirked slightly, watching as Stormbreaker's frustration grew.
The man was clearly tracking his sword's condition, calculating whether he could end the fight before his weapon gave out.
But every second that passed, the balance tilted further and further against him. At times, Stormbreaker even jumped back, creating distance—and it was obvious.
He was getting desperate.
And the worst part? Broken wasn't even breaking a sweat.
His relaxed expression was a constant reminder that this fight had turned into a countdown to Stormbreaker's loss.
"Damn it," Stormbreaker cursed under his breath, his frustration clear as day on the big screen.
The audience was growing restless, eagerly waiting for the battle's conclusion.
At first, most of them had been certain that Stormbreaker would dominate—but now? That expectation was falling apart.
"What's going on? Why hasn't Stormbreaker finished this fight yet?"
"I mean, I can see that he's fighting with incredible technique—he's landed multiple hits on Broken."
"Yeah, but look at Broken—he's just casually parrying everything, and his Health hasn't dropped at all."
"Actually, neither of them have lost any Health."

"Damn, Broken really has way too many tricks up his sleeve. First, it was that pickaxe that solved puzzles instantly, and now this weird-looking greatsword that somehow isn't breaking, no matter how many times it gets hit."
"Yeah, and Stormbreaker is actually hesitating now. I really want to know what's actually happening."
On the big screen, it was now clear as day— The fight had completely stalled.
Stormbreaker was no longer in an offensive stance, even though Broken was still standing calmly in a parry position.
The tension hung in the air.
Then, Stormbreaker's voice echoed throughout the arena, reaching every spectator.
"What kind of greatsword is that?"
Broken remained unfazed, his expression relaxed.
"It's just a normal greatsword," he replied casually.
That single exchange only fueled the crowd's curiosity further.
And finally—everyone started to realize the truth. Stormbreaker wasn't hesitating for no reason. He was hesitating because of Broken's greatsword.
Then, Stormbreaker spoke again, confirming everyone's suspicions.
"My sword's durability is dropping like crazy... Is that a special skill attached to your greatsword?"
The moment those words left his mouth, the entire stadium erupted in murmurs. The mystery was finally solved.
At the casters' desk, Brando immediately reacted.
"Oh! Looks like we've uncovered yet another trick from Broken's arsenal!"
His excitement was obvious.

"A greatsword that rapidly drains an opponent's weapon durability?! That's absolutely terrifying. We all know how expensive it is to craft and enhance high-tier weapons. If your weapon gets destroyed in a fight like this, you'd think twice before going up against Broken's greatsword again!"
Then, he turned to Paul.
"What do you think?"
Paul simply smirked and folded his arms.
"Well... I think we already know who's winning this match."
With that, the crowd's attention snapped back to the big screen, where the battle's outcome was now all but decided.
At that exact moment, Stormbreaker withdrew his sword and raised both hands.
And just like that—
A notification flashed across the big screen, signaling the end of the match!
Broken wins!

But once again, in a way that left everyone speechless. This time, he didn't win by finishing the fight in record time like his previous matches. Instead, he forced his opponent to surrender after a grueling battle.

The entire stadium erupted—some in cheers, others in disbelief. This was the most anticlimactic result they could have imagined. Stormbreaker, the clear favorite, with his insane abilities, had been expected to dominate...
Yet, in the end, he chose to surrender.
The two players stepped out of their capsule devices, and the host immediately stepped in, standing between them.
Stormbreaker grabbed the mic first.
"That wasn't exactly a satisfying fight," he admitted. "But I have to give it to Broken—he's got a lot of tricks up his sleeve."
His eyes narrowed slightly, his expression unreadable.
"I'll be coming for payback next time."
The host jumped in with an enthusiastic response.
"Oh, I'm sure everyone here knows that Team Broken and Team Stormbreaker are set to clash again in the final Raid Race! Who's excited for round two?"
The crowd roared in approval, hyped for their inevitable rematch.
Finally, Broken took the mic, his tone as composed as ever.
"I learned a lot from this battle. Thanks for the lesson."
As always, he kept it humble—just like before.
The first match of the day was finally over.
And with that, Broken's rank climbed even higher, preparing him for his next fight later that evening.
Since his schedule left him with several hours to spare, he decided to use the time efficiently.
Logging back into Immortal Legacy, SexyGrill hadn't returned to the game yet.
So instead—
He entered the Moonlight Dimension, aiming to climb even higher in the Tower Trial.
Upon stepping onto the beautiful and serene floating island, a familiar presence greeted him. Cecilia appeared beside him, her ethereal form glowing softly in the moonlit space.
"How does it feel being here alone, Cecil?" he asked as he walked forward, the guardian spirit floating by his side.
"Alone? That is not something I concern myself with, my Lord..."
Right...
She was a spirit now, wasn't she?
From what he had learned from Polly and Gaia, spirits had emotions—but perhaps they experienced time differently. Maybe waiting in solitude wasn't as tedious for them as it would be for humans.
But as Broken conversed with Cecilia, another thought surfaced in his mind—
Something he had kept stored away, unsure what to do with it. Because so far, it had shown no changes since the day he obtained it.
Reaching into his Inventory, he pulled out the Dormant Fae Seed.
It was the result of Elaine's death—two Soul Stones that had merged into one entity.
The object resembled a large egg, roughly the size of an adult human head. But unlike a regular egg, it was wrapped in a green cocoon-like shell, giving it an almost organic, pulsing appearance.
Broken had long wondered—
Would Elaine be reborn from this seed? Or would it result in something completely new, like how Pawpaw had come into existence?

He had already tried infusing his mana into it multiple times before, but nothing had ever happened. Considering that Elaine was a faery with a deep affinity for nature, he had even brought the egg to different natural environments, hoping it would trigger some kind of reaction.
Still—no changes.
But for some reason—
Right now, he felt like trying again.
Without overthinking it, he placed his hand on the egg's surface and channeled his mana into it. He had no expectations.
But then—
For the first time ever—
A notification appeared!
[You have supplied mana to the Seed.]
What?!

chapters.title: Chapter 779 - The Seed Awakens
paragraphs: [You have supplied mana to the Seed.]
Broken froze, his eyes locked onto the notification in front of him.
Like hell! The seed finally responded?!
But why now? He had tried this countless times before, even right here in the Moonlight Dimension, and nothing had happened.
Now, suddenly—it was working?
The progress bar ticked up to 1%, confirming that the Seed was developing. And if he kept at it, it would eventually hatch, bringing a new creature into existence.
Whatever it was.

But based on his experience with Pawpaw, one thing was certain—this was going to be a powerful addition to his forces. Whether it was Elaine, a reincarnation of her, or something entirely new, Broken knew one thing—
Elaine had been incredibly powerful in life. If this Seed carried even a fraction of her strength, then whatever hatched from it would be nothing short of extraordinary.
All he had to do was keep supplying mana. That should be simple enough. So, without hesitation, he channeled his mana into the Seed again.
But this time—
The notification that appeared was not what he expected.
[The Seed has begun to awaken, but it is not yours alone to nurture. It must be nourished by the one who walks beside you, bound by nature's embrace.]
Broken furrowed his brow as he read the new notification, trying to decipher its meaning. It was vague, yet strangely specific at the same time.
Why had the Seed only started responding now? He had tried countless times before, and nothing had happened. But then—A thought crossed his mind.
He had never attempted to supply mana again after his marriage to Alora. And now, the system message hinted at needing someone who walks beside him?!
Did that mean...? Did he need to nurture the Seed with his partner? With his wife?
Broken paused, thinking back to Pawpaw's egg—how it had required mana from specific individuals to hatch. At the time, the only person who met the requirements had been Alora.
And now—
It was happening again.
But there was a problem. Alora wasn't here. Which meant he had no choice but to wait until he returned to the capital. Who knew when that would be?
He sighed.
Sure, he could teleport back to the capital city of Dissidia Kingdom anytime. But doing so would mean traveling all the way back here afterward.
And without knowing whether the Seed would demand something else next, it wasn't worth the gamble. For now—he had to put this on hold.
Broken returned the Seed to his inventory, deciding to revisit the matter later.
For now, his focus shifted to the Tower Trial. Without wasting more time, he made his way to the trial grounds and soon found himself stepping into the next challenge—the 11th floor.
Time passed. Several attempts later...
He still hadn't achieved the results he wanted.
And now, he was once again outside the tower, standing in the open space where Cecilia awaited him with her usual gentle smile.
"You're doing great, Master." Her voice was calm, reassuring. "That was a lot better than before."

"Thanks, Cecil..." Broken exhaled, rolling his shoulders. "I know that, but it looks like I need to increase my training if I want to keep progressing through the tower. This is taking way too much time."
At his words, Cecilia's expression softened with concern.
"You have all the time in the world to complete your challenges. I will always be here to accompany you."
Broken chuckled, shaking his head.
With nothing else left to do in the Moonlight Dimension, he decided to log out of the area. And yeah—outside, it was already night, just like it had been inside the Moonlight Dimension moments ago.
He was back in the forest, standing in the same place where he had been before entering the Moonlight Dimension. Now, all he had to do was wait—SexyGrill would be logging in soon.
But then—
The same sensation hit him again.
A massive gust of wind tore through the forest, rattling the branches and even the massive trees around him.
Broken instantly recognized this. He knew what was coming. And just as expected—
The same monster.
A Wyvern.
Its wings beat furiously as it dove over the forest canopy, its sheer presence stirring the forest awake from its slumber.
Broken should hide and wait for it to leave. That's what he and SexyGrill had done last time. And it was exactly what she had recommended.
But this time—
He hesitated.
Because last time, he had regretted letting it go. A high-level, Epic-grade monster like this? Who wouldn't be tempted to take it down?
Still, SexyGrill's warning lingered in his mind—
The possibility that killing it could draw in more Wyverns. And the challenge of fighting it in midair? That wouldn't be easy either.
But then again—
If this Wyvern was going to keep circling this area, wouldn't it be better if he at least tested its strength first?
Just in case a situation arose where he had no choice but to fight it. Right? Yes. That was a perfectly reasonable excuse.
[Eternal Flame - Grim Reaper (Conditional Active Skill) activated]

Broken knew exactly what he needed to do. It had been a while since he last used this skill, but now was the perfect moment. The timing was ideal—night had already fallen, and this ability could only be activated under the moonlight.
An overpowered ability, indeed, though it came with certain limitations.
As shadows swallowed his body, he transformed into his Grim Reaper form, seamlessly merging into the surrounding darkness.
This form granted him a significant advantage—Along with it came a Legendary-grade weapon: The Soul Drainer.
Without hesitation, Broken wielded both the Golden Bow of Artemis and the scythe. He placed the scythe onto the bow, using it as an arrow, before beginning to charge his attack.

The greatest benefit of this combination? He didn't need to retrieve the weapon manually after firing. Once launched, it would return on its own, allowing him to fire, assess the damage, and retreat back into the shadows.
[Explosive Arrow (Active Skill) Lv. 6 activated]

At that moment, from behind him—A portal ripped open, revealing a towering figure. A massive Grim Reaper, several times larger than Broken, emerged, gripping an identical scythe in its skeletal hands.
Let's see...
Would this attack instantly kill the Wyvern?

Broken froze, his eyes locked onto the notification in front of him.
Like hell!
The seed finally responded?!
But why now?
He had tried this countless times before, even right here in the Moonlight Dimension, and nothing had happened.
Now, suddenly—it was working?
The progress bar ticked up to 1%, confirming that the Seed was developing.
And if he kept at it, it would eventually hatch, bringing a new creature into existence.
Whatever it was.
But based on his experience with Pawpaw, one thing was certain—this was going to be a powerful addition to his forces.
Whether it was Elaine, a reincarnation of her, or something entirely new, Broken knew one thing—
Elaine had been incredibly powerful in life.
If this Seed carried even a fraction of her strength, then whatever hatched from it would be nothing short of extraordinary.
All he had to do was keep supplying mana.
That should be simple enough.
So, without hesitation, he channeled his mana into the Seed again.
But this time—
The notification that appeared was not what he expected.
[The Seed has begun to awaken, but it is not yours alone to nurture.

Broken furrowed his brow as he read the new notification, trying to decipher its meaning.
It was vague, yet strangely specific at the same time.
Why had the Seed only started responding now?
He had tried countless times before, and nothing had happened.
But then—A thought crossed his mind.
He had never attempted to supply mana again after his marriage to Alora.
And now, the system message hinted at needing someone who walks beside him?!
Did that mean...?
Did he need to nurture the Seed with his partner?
With his wife?
Broken paused, thinking back to Pawpaw's egg—how it had required mana from specific individuals to hatch.
At the time, the only person who met the requirements had been Alora.
And now—
It was happening again.
But there was a problem.
Alora wasn't here.
Which meant he had no choice but to wait until he returned to the capital.
Who knew when that would be?
He sighed.
Sure, he could teleport back to the capital city of Dissidia Kingdom anytime.
But doing so would mean traveling all the way back here afterward.
And without knowing whether the Seed would demand something else next, it wasn't worth the gamble.
For now—he had to put this on hold.
Broken returned the Seed to his inventory, deciding to revisit the matter later.
For now, his focus shifted to the Tower Trial.

Time passed.
Several attempts later...
He still hadn't achieved the results he wanted.
And now, he was once again outside the tower, standing in the open space where Cecilia awaited him with her usual gentle smile.
"You're doing great, Master." Her voice was calm, reassuring.
"That was a lot better than before."
"Thanks, Cecil..." Broken exhaled, rolling his shoulders.
"I know that, but it looks like I need to increase my training if I want to keep progressing through the tower.
This is taking way too much time."
At his words, Cecilia's expression softened with concern.
"You have all the time in the world to complete your challenges.

chapters.title: Chapter 780 - Broken's Arrow Strikes
paragraphs: The wyvern did not leave immediately; instead, it kept circling the area near where Broken was. It was almost as if the creature knew there was an intruder nearby. Or was that just his assumption?

Still, he couldn't shake the thought—could this wyvern have some kind of connection to the Dragonkin? In fact, Dragonkin were considered inferior when compared to true dragons. But for some reason, the similarities and the close ties between these three creatures intrigued Broken.
But then, what exactly was the relationship between dragons and Dragonkin?

According to Yunatea's history, Dragonkin were merely a subset of the beastkin race, which was widespread across the land. Beastkin, however, was not part of the seven major races of Yunatea. Even so, everyone knew that their numbers should technically rank second, right after humans.
At least, within Yunatea.
If one were to consider the bigger picture, the most numerous race would still be demons. However, most demons reside in Hell rather than in Yunatea.
And wyverns? They were classified as monsters—or, more precisely, creatures lacking intelligence.

The charging time for the skill was complete. Broken released the bowstring, and the scythe shot forward. A powerful gust of wind surged alongside an explosion of shadow energy. At the same time, an ethereal figure of the Grim Reaper behind him, shrouded in darkness, and lunged forward with terrifying speed.
It was as if Death itself had descended upon the world, ready to claim its next victim.

The spectral form of the Grim Reaper streaked through the air, heading straight for the wyvern. The very moment it made contact, a massive slash tore through the sky, followed by a violent eruption of shadow energy. The impact triggered a series of successive explosions, shaking the entire forest to its core.
Oh. Broken had not expected the blast to be this intense—it would definitely wake up more of the forest's inhabitants.
The wyvern lost its balance, flung backward by the sheer force of the attack.
But damn! Even that wasn't enough to kill it. And this should have been... an absolutely devastating hit.

Still, it was clear that the wyvern was struggling to stay airborne. Its movements had become erratic, and it was flying at a much faster pace—almost as if it had lost control of its momentum. Without hesitation, it veered off, heading deeper into the forest and toward the mountainous region beyond.
Should he give chase?
If he pursued it and landed a few more strikes, he could probably finish it off. But the wyvern was already far ahead, its right wing nearly torn in half.
With a quiet exhale, Broken deactivated his Eternal Flame Form.
"You've been caught," a voice suddenly spoke up behind him.
Broken turned his head to see SexyGrill standing there.
She let out a sigh and stepped closer, saying nothing—just waiting for him to explain what he had done.
"Surely, you know this is going to cause some trouble, right?" he said casually.
She sighed again, then chuckled softly, lowering her gaze for a moment. It was as if she found the situation amusing. Once satisfied, she looked up at him again.
"Seriously, though, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't getting bored of just hunting monsters during our travels. A bit of trouble might actually make things more interesting."
"That's some quality sarcasm, Grill," Broken remarked as he turned away. With a flick of his wrist, he summoned Polly and Blaze. He climbed onto Blaze's back, while SexyGrill hopped onto Polly.

They continued their journey through the night, trying to cover as much distance as possible while time was still on their side. After all, this journey couldn't go on forever. It had already been so long since Ivana left—so long without a single trace of her whereabouts.
Broken's only hope was to find the Dragonkin, hoping they could provide answers—or at the very least, a clue he could follow.
But...
"Grill, tell me. How big are our chances of actually finding the Dragonkin?"
SexyGrill didn't answer right away. Instead, she turned to him with a grin.

"I have no idea," she admitted. "We can only try and hope they're kind enough to show themselves. Or, who knows? Maybe things will get a little tense, we'll have to survive their attacks for a while, and then—if we're lucky—we might actually get to talk to them."
"That sounds like so much fun." Broken's tone was dripping with sarcasm.

"According to the information I had gathered, there were several rumored locations where encounters with Dragonkin had occurred—deep within these forests and mountains. But no one truly knew where the Dragonkin resided."
This was the only clue Broken had—the image of a mountain range engraved on Ivana's bracelet. It was the same mountain range they were heading toward.
And then there was the Dragonkin. They had to be connected to her in some way. After all, Ivana's identity as the Dragon Princess had already been confirmed.
Now, it was only a matter of time—whether it took weeks or even months. He would stay as long as it took to find the next clue that could lead him to Ivana's whereabouts.

A deafening roar echoed through the air, followed by the massive form of a creature crashing violently into the ground. It tumbled uncontrollably, slamming into the rocky cliffs above before finally coming to a halt.
It was the dead of night, the dense forest shrouded in darkness.
The creature lifted its head weakly—it was a wyvern, its right wing badly wounded. It opened its mouth repeatedly, letting out desperate cries, either in pain or as a call for help.
The wyvern struggled to flap its injured wing, but the damage had only worsened. The limb twitched, barely responding to its efforts.
"What happened...?"
A deep, heavy voice rang out from the shadows.

Figures emerged from the darkness—three of them. Their armor gleamed under the moonlight, forged from obsidian-like stone, dark and imposing. But the most striking feature about them was the pair of wings extending from their backs.
The trio rushed toward the fallen wyvern, surrounding it with concern, their expressions sharp with curiosity and alarm.
"The wyvern is badly wounded," one of them muttered.
"Yeah, and from the looks of it, this was caused by a single attack—something with massive destructive power."
"What kind of force could deal this much damage?"
"Someone hunting in the forest."

"Damn it... those foolish little creatures always push their limits." The third figure clenched their fists before turning to the others. "Alert the tribe leader. We're going to find whoever did this."

chapters.title: Chapter 781 - The Forgotten Kin
paragraphs: Eternal Challenge.

The grand competition had truly drawn an overwhelming amount of excitement and attention, especially with so many top players from Immortal Legacy gathering in one place. It dominated social media discussions and was frequently covered on television, becoming a daily hot topic.
And yet... all of that was lost on Leon. He only showed up when it was time for his matches, then vanished again, consumed by his responsibilities that refused to wait.

His life had become a never-ending cycle of movement, leaving no room for even a moment of rest. Sometimes, he wondered if he was pushing himself too hard. But at the same time, he felt like he still didn't have enough time—there was always more to accomplish, and he was nowhere near done.
Leon walked alongside King, heading toward the stadium where his next event awaited—The Blacksmith Competition. It was bound to take up a significant portion of his day.

Having King beside him was a rare relief. Normally, all eyes would be glued to Leon, but today, the presence of his bodyguard divided their attention. People hesitated—unsure whether they should approach or greet him.

So this was what it felt like to finally use his wealth for something useful. Just hiring a single bodyguard had changed his life dramatically. Should he take it further? Maybe hire ten more? Surround himself from all sides until no one could even see him?

There was also an interview scheduled for later—something Leon was honestly tempted to skip. He had already turned it down three times before, but it seemed he wouldn't be able to avoid it any longer. Worse, it was a talk show-style segment hosted by a well-known figure in the Immortal Legacy community.
Wouldn't it be easier if they just conducted the talk show inside the game?
That way, he could sit there in his Invincible Paragon Armor, his face completely hidden behind the helmet. No need to fake a smile just because a camera was pointed at him.
Leon and King finally entered the participants' lounge, where rows of seats were lined up. A few of his friends were already there, chatting amongst themselves.
Then, a man with blond hair and sunglasses waved at him.
It was Maylon.
Leon and King joined him, settling in to watch whatever match was currently taking place that day.

The real reason Leon had arrived early at the stadium this time was because he wanted to discuss a few things with Maylon. That was why, the moment he sat down beside him, everything around him—the noise, the excitement of the arena—instantly faded into the background.
"Any progress on your journey? Have you found any trace of the Dragonkin?" Maylon asked, getting straight to the point.

Maylon was the kind of person who disliked small talk—one of the reasons Leon enjoyed discussing things with him. Their conversations were always direct, focused only on what truly mattered. Maylon had a sharp sense for filtering out unnecessary details, making every discussion efficient and worthwhile.
"Not yet..." Leon replied in a low voice. "But I did come across a high-level Epic-grade Wyvern roaming around."
He paused before asking, "So, do you have any important updates?
Maylon leaned forward slightly, clearly eager to share his information. "I got a report from my scout—someone spotted Dragonkin in the Central Continent."
"The Central Continent?"

The fact that Dragonkin were already considered extremely rare made this a significant revelation. And the last known sightings of Dragonkin had been on the Western Continent, particularly in the same places they had once lived. That alone had raised countless questions.
Because... According to history, their race had been slaughtered long ago by the High Elves. It all tied back to how the High Elf Queen had once hunted down the Dragon Princess.

And yet, despite everything, Ivana had somehow survived. She had lived in hiding with Gia until the moment Broken unlocked her true identity—right when there seemed to be no way out in their battle against Focalor.
"In large numbers?" Leon asked.
"No, just one... and it was spotted inside the High Elf castle," Maylon replied.
Leon immediately turned to him. That information did not sit right with him.
"Shouldn't the Dragonkin hate the High Elves? Then why would one be there?"
"I think this is a similar case to how there's a dragon in the High Elf palace, right?" Maylon pointed out.
Leon nodded.
The High Elf Queen had a dragon serving as her guardian—a creature even rarer than Dragonkin. No one truly knew how many dragons still existed in Yunatea.
One thing was certain: Ivana was still alive, still carrying the royal bloodline of dragons. What that meant for Yunatea's future remained an open question.

"Dragons," Maylon continued, "after being nearly wiped out, their royal family was slaughtered—leaving only the Dragon Princess alive. After that, the remaining dragons were enslaved by the High Elf Queen. And that's the reality we're dealing with now."
That was why the High Elves continued to dominate—not just in the Central Continent, but across others as well. The mere presence of their queen instilled fear everywhere.
For two reasons:
One, her Blessing as the Pride Champion, which gave her the ability to alter reality itself.
Two, the fact that she controlled the dragons.
Leon exhaled slowly, processing Maylon's words. "Are you saying that after wiping out the Dragonkin, the Queen enslaved the survivors—just like she did with the dragons?
"That," Maylon said, "would be the most logical explanation."
Leon sat in silence, deep in thought.
What he was really considering was whether it was worth it to search for the Dragonkin in the West Continent, especially if there was a chance they were affiliated with the High Elf Queen.
And even if he decided to go after them, how long would it take? How many weeks—months—would he need to search the vast forests and mountain ranges for any trace of the Dragonkin?
Even with his Flying Golem tirelessly scanning the area, it was still a slow process. It could take forever.
Should he build more? Maybe four Flying Golems—maxing out the number of constructs he could control—to increase his search efficiency? Because if he didn't, this search might never end.
"Tell me again, Maylon... do you have a better alternative for finding Ivana?" Leon asked.

Maylon shook his head slowly. "My bet is still on finding the Dragonkin..." He hesitated for a moment before continuing. "For some reason, I still believe that some of them survived the High Elf Queen's purge. And if they did, they're likely waiting for the right time to take their revenge."
He exhaled sharply. "There's always the possibility that most of the Dragonkin are already under the Queen's control... but we don't have another option."
He sighed. "And with our current strength, I'd say the smartest thing we can do is avoid crossing paths with the High Elf Queen at all costs."

Leon nodded slowly, fully aware of how dire their situation would become if they ended up facing the one person responsible for the near-extinction of dragons—the same ruler who now held absolute power over Yunatea.
Maylon suddenly stood up, stretching his arms. "I have to go do a hellishly boring match. See you later."
He stepped away from his seat, leaving the chair beside Leon empty—at least for a moment.
Then, someone else approached.
"Leon... I'll join you here."
He turned his head and saw a woman with black hair walking toward him.

Leon exhaled slowly, processing Maylon's words.
"Are you saying that after wiping out the Dragonkin, the Queen enslaved the survivors—just like she did with the dragons?
"That," Maylon said, "would be the most logical explanation."
Leon sat in silence, deep in thought.
What he was really considering was whether it was worth it to search for the Dragonkin in the West Continent, especially if there was a chance they were affiliated with the High Elf Queen.
And even if he decided to go after them, how long would it take?
How many weeks—months—would he need to search the vast forests and mountain ranges for any trace of the Dragonkin?
Even with his Flying Golem tirelessly scanning the area, it was still a slow process.
It could take forever.
Should he build more?
Maybe four Flying Golems—maxing out the number of constructs he could control—to increase his search efficiency?
Because if he didn't, this search might never end.
"Tell me again, Maylon... do you have a better alternative for finding Ivana?" Leon asked.
Maylon shook his head slowly.
"My bet is still on finding the Dragonkin..." He hesitated for a moment before continuing.
"For some reason, I still believe that some of them survived the High Elf Queen's purge.
And if they did, they're likely waiting for the right time to take their revenge."
He exhaled sharply.
"There's always the possibility that most of the Dragonkin are already under the Queen's control... but we don't have another option."
He sighed.
"And with our current strength, I'd say the smartest thing we can do is avoid crossing paths with the High Elf Queen at all costs."

Leon nodded slowly, fully aware of how dire their situation would become if they ended up facing the one person responsible for the near-extinction of dragons—the same ruler who now held absolute power over Yunatea.
Maylon suddenly stood up, stretching his arms.
"I have to go do a hellishly boring match.
See you later."
He stepped away from his seat, leaving the chair beside Leon empty—at least for a moment.
Then, someone else approached.
"Leon...
I'll join you here."
He turned his head and saw a woman with black hair walking toward him.

chapters.title: Chapter 782 - The Tournament Heats Up
paragraphs: It was Euna.

The girl smiled at him as she took the seat beside Leon, leaning back with effortless grace. Her posture was relaxed—elegant, even. She always carried herself with a natural air of confidence, something that set her apart.

It wasn't surprising. Euna and her brother came from an incredibly wealthy family—just how rich, Leon had no idea. The difference was that, while Freya was also from money, she never made it obvious. She kept a low profile, never flaunting her status in front of others.

Meanwhile, Euna and Booyoung? They embraced the glamour. Everything about them—from their clothing to the accessories they wore—screamed luxury. And honestly, Leon wasn't even sure how expensive half the things they owned actually were.
"Today is the Blacksmith Competition, right?" Euna asked.
"Yes... and it's going to take a long time," he replied. "The worst part is that whatever I craft during the competition won't carry over into the game. That makes it feel pretty pointless."
"Well, at the very least, you'll win a huge cash prize if you take first place, right?" she said with a smile. "Not to mention, I heard from Freya that you landed quite a big sponsor for this event."
Leon let out a small chuckle, nodding. "Yeah... I guess that's the only reason I'm still bothering to compete."
Euna nudged his shoulder playfully. "Come on, champion—get a little more excited. You're going to gain tons of popularity from this."
"Like my popularity isn't already big enough to bring me more problems?" he said dryly.
She laughed. "Gather more money, trust me—it's fun."
Leon hummed in thought. The idea of accumulating more wealth was already forming in his mind. Especially since he had been considering getting his own place—a personal building entirely for himself.
Somewhere he could base all his operations. Somewhere that had everything he needed in one place.
Maybe even a space for King.
And who knew? If things went well, he might even recruit more people to work for him in the future.
"We might end up facing each other in the semifinals," Euna said casually.
Leon turned to her, momentarily caught off guard when she met his gaze at the exact same moment.
For a brief second, he was acutely aware of just how close they were speaking—close enough for him to take in every detail of her face.
It was... almost blinding.

Everything about Euna exuded luxury—her hairstyle, her earrings, even the subtle touch of makeup she wore. Each detail looked flawless, expensive in a way that made him wonder just how much effort (and money) went into her appearance.
Leon quickly averted his gaze, breaking eye contact.
"Semifinals of Duel of Champions?" he asked.
Euna nodded with a confident smile. "Yes. That is... if I win my bracket first. But I'm sure we'll meet in the semifinals."
Leon smirked at her confidence. "That's good."
"Oh?"
"I'll finally get to pay you back for what you did to me when we first met," he said.

That made Euna laugh—really laugh. She lowered her head slightly, clearly amused by his words. "Oh? Then make sure you give it your best shot—because if it's not you who makes it to the semifinals, I'll lose interest in the match."
"I will," Leon said, his grin widening. "Because I promised I'd pay you back for what you did back then."
Euna laughed again, shaking her head. "I thought that grudge was already over?"
"Oh, it is." Leon leaned back. "But revenge is still necessary."
They both chuckled, the tension between them fading into something light and easy. For the first time in a while, Leon felt relaxed—swept up in the warmth of their banter.
"Good," Euna said, her eyes gleaming with challenge. "I'll be waiting for your revenge. Make sure it's devastating—because I won't be holding back."
In yet another interview, this time led by Brando, a well-known host within the Immortal Legacy community, all cameras were focused on a single guest.
Seated across from Brando was a player heavily favored to win the next big competition happening later that day.
"We have Lanceshot with us today!" Brando announced enthusiastically.
The man in question flashed a wide grin and waved at the camera.
"Well, Lanceshot, I heard you recently achieved Expert Rank Blacksmith status. That's quite an impressive achievement!"

"Yeah," Lanceshot replied confidently. "I've been dominating the Blacksmith Leaderboards for years now. In fact, I was the first player to ever reach Expert Rank in blacksmithing! That makes me the undisputed best blacksmith with the highest potential. I'm sure this achievement will take me to the very top of Yunatea. I mean, with my skills and expertise, it's only a matter of time before major factions and royal courts start offering me positions as an official kingdom blacksmith.

Brando clapped, clearly entertained. "I'd love to see you reach even greater heights in Yunatea! Especially since we all know there's already a blacksmith who managed to rise to the rank of King in a kingdom on the Southern Continent."
"Broken, huh? Haha." Lanceshot chuckled. "Well, he's not a pure blacksmith. He's a fighter who just happens to have Blacksmith as a class. So, we're not even in the same league."
He leaned back with a smug grin.

"While I have dedicated my entire in-game time to mastering blacksmithing, Broken? Who knows what he's been doing? Haha. But honestly, we shouldn't even be bringing up Broken in a serious discussion about top-tier blacksmiths."
Brando leaned forward, his expression turning serious.
"But Lanceshot, weren't you in the same competition as Broken back in Dissidia, when he managed to craft a Legendary-grade spear?"
"I knew you'd bring that up." Lanceshot exhaled sharply, shaking his head.

"Yeah, I was there... and I almost won. If it hadn't been for that ridiculous stroke of luck that just happened to favor Broken... Well, let's be real—hard work always beats luck. And honestly? There's no point in crafting a single Legendary-grade item if you're just going to be stuck making low-tier gear afterward, right?"
He shrugged, then leaned back with an air of confidence.
"Meanwhile, I know the most effective way to craft the best items in Yunatea. And no, that's not bragging—it's just fact. My track record speaks for itself."
Brando smirked. "So... you're confident that you'll win the Blacksmith Competition this time?"
"That's not even a question." Lanceshot grinned.

"And I'll prove it in this competition. If Broken actually thinks he can win the same event twice, then he's just wasting his spot by entering. Honestly, he should've just signed up for the Beast Battle instead. That would suit him way better—hiding behind his summons, as always."
Lanceshot chuckled, shaking his head. "That's more his style. Hahaha."
Brando clapped his hands, laughing in response to Lanceshot's confident remarks.

"Yeah, sure! I have no doubt this is going to be an exciting competition. A lot of people are eager to see what kind of incredible items the participants will craft this time. Who knows... maybe we'll even see another Legendary-grade item appear. Anything is possible."
Then, turning toward the camera, Brando flashed a charismatic smile.
"Stay tuned! Because up next, we'll be talking with Broken—and trust me, this is our chance to dig deeper into who he really is."
With that, Brando and Lanceshot shook hands, wrapping up their conversation for this segment.

chapters.title: Chapter 783 - Don't Make Us Do It Again
paragraphs: "We have Broken with us today!" Brando announced enthusiastically as Leon settled into his seat across from him.
The cameras zoomed in on Leon's face as he did his best to force a smile, giving a small wave toward the viewers.
Hopefully, that was a convincing enough smile.

For the first time, he realized that being on camera, knowing thousands—maybe millions—were watching, wasn't as easy as it looked. The pressure felt real, and instead of helping him relax like usual, it made him feel tense.
"Thanks for having me today, Brando," Leon said, keeping his voice steady.

"Oh, that's so humble of you, huh?" Brando grinned. "I mean, let's be real—you've been putting on some insane performances in past competitions. I was there, and whoa! You pulled off miracle after miracle! That was incredible—and honestly? I'm looking forward to seeing more of that magic today."
Leon nodded, offering a polite smile. "Thanks for the compliments. I just hope my performance in the Blacksmith Competition won't disappoint your expectations."

Brando laughed, clapping his hands together. "But surely, Broken—okay, okay, I know this interview is supposed to be about the competition. But... this is a rare opportunity, and I'm not going to waste it."
Brando leaned forward, a mischievous glint in his eyes.
"So, my question is... and yeah, I'm not holding back—tell me how you ended up marrying Queen Alora."
Then, he dramatically paused, his face shifting into an exaggerated expression of shock before turning toward the camera.
"I'm sure this is the question that's been on everyone's minds, right? I know you all watching at home want to hear the answer to this one, don't you?"
Leon forced a smile.
He had expected this question to come up—he knew it was only a matter of time. The problem was, this time, he couldn't avoid it like he usually did with surprise interviews.

Leon had learned a lot about handling public conversations over the past few months. Being around friends who came from wealthy, high-profile backgrounds had taught him a thing or two—people like Heejin, a celebrity who lived in the spotlight, or Euna, who carried herself with effortless confidence as someone from an extremely wealthy family.

He knew very well that even now, there were still many people who disliked what had happened in the game. After all, he had taken Alora, a woman worshipped by thousands—perhaps millions—as their untouchable goddess... and made her his wife.
That alone had shattered the illusions of many who had dreamed of being with her, idolizing her as though she were a divine figure beyond reach.
And it wasn't just about her beauty—it was everything. Alora's unmatched power, her flawless reputation, and her mystique had made her one of the most talked-about figures online.
The High Elf Queen held the top spot as the most admired and feared figure in Immortal Legacy—a ruler both stunningly beautiful and unbelievably powerful.
Alora was second.
And recently, Ivana's popularity had been rapidly rising—especially after she revealed her Dragon form.

People were still speculating about what kind of dragon she truly was. Some even theorized that she was connected to the Dragon Princess, though without solid confirmation, it remained a rumor for now.
Still, that speculation alone had boosted Ivana's status to third place, right below Alora.
Now, Leon was ready to answer the question. He knew his response would likely make even more people hate him.
Well... he didn't really care.
As long as they kept their complaints online, it didn't matter to him.
And if anyone actually tried to confront him in person? Well, he had King—his massive, powerhouse of a bodyguard—ready to shut that down instantly.

Yeah, Leon could fight too—especially that he had started training in martial arts and pushing his physical limits further than ever before. But he wasn't the kind of guy who would bother responding to something like this with violence.
Still, he understood—this wasn't a simple issue for a lot of people. Which meant... he needed to give them an answer that would be as satisfying as possible.
Leon exhaled slowly, his forced smile shifting into something more composed—calculated. He leaned forward slightly, resting his elbows on the armrests of his chair, and looked directly at Brando.

"You know... I get why people are curious about this," he began, his tone steady but firm. "From the outside, it probably looks like I just appeared out of nowhere and suddenly ended up with Queen Alora. But the truth is, that's far from everything people think they know."
He let those words sink in before continuing.
"I didn't just meet her and suddenly decide, 'Hey, let's get married.' No. We fought together. We bled together. We survived together."
The energy in the room shifted. Brando, usually quick to jump in, stayed silent, letting him speak.

"I went through countless battles by her side. We faced things together that most people will never even hear about—because some fights aren't meant for public stories. And for a long time, I wasn't sure what she meant to me. I wasn't looking for power. I wasn't looking for fame. But when you've stood next to someone through life and death, when you've trusted each other in ways no one else could understand... that's where the bond forms."

Leon let out a quiet chuckle, shaking his head. "And you know what? I don't expect everyone to accept that. I don't expect people to be happy about it. But there's something you all need to understand."
He leaned forward, his gaze unwavering.
"Following the passing of King Alorik, only two individuals now bear the Golden Paragon."
The room seemed to still hear those words.
"And those two people... are her and me."
Leon let the weight of that statement settle in before sighing and sitting back.

"So I get it. I get that some people are upset. I get that some people want to lash out—at her, at me, even at the Dissidia Kingdom itself—just because they think things should have gone differently. But let me make something very, very clear—stop troubling Dissidia."
His voice was calm, but there was steel in his tone.
"In-game or out of it, if you still think it's a good idea to come after her, then fine. But know this—you're not just facing her. You're facing me. And you're facing the Vensalor Guild."
Leon's gaze flickered to the camera, his expression unwavering.
"We stood before the gates of Dissidia once before to teach a lesson to those who tried. Don't make us do it again."
Brando let out a slow exhale, visibly taken aback by Leon's answer. Then, he chuckled before shaking his head.

"Well... damn." He leaned back in his chair. "You guys heard him, right? I mean... I'm not saying you have to like it, but let's be real—if Broken and Vensalor are standing at the Dissidia gates, that's not exactly a fight most people can walk away from in one piece."
Brando turned back to Leon, a knowing grin on his face.

"And honestly? That's probably the most straightforward warning we've ever had on this show. So, for all the hotheads out there still trying to make this an issue... well, consider yourselves warned."
He clapped his hands together, shifting gears smoothly.

"Now then! Before we start a war in the comment sections, let's move on to something just as intense—because next up, we're diving straight into one of the biggest competitions of this event. That's right, folks—The Blacksmith Competition is about to begin! And guess what? Broken himself is competing."
"So, stay tuned because after this break, we're going to witness some of the best crafters in Yunatea go head-to-head."
"Will we see another Legendary-grade item appear?"
"Will Lanceshot's confidence hold up against the competition?"
"And more importantly..."
"Will Broken prove that he's more than just a fighter?"
"You don't wanna miss this. We'll be right back!"

Don't make us do it again."

"You don't wanna miss this.

chapters.title: Chapter 784 - Who Needs the Leaderboard?
paragraphs: The atmosphere was electric.
Leon hadn't expected the Blacksmith Crafting Competition to draw such a massive crowd. The stadium was nearly 60% full—an impressive turnout for an event like this.
It was honestly shocking.
Then again, it wasn't just one competition happening at the moment. The stadium had multiple stages, each hosting different contests at the same time.
Still, it just so happened that as soon as the Blacksmith Competition was about to begin, the audience started pouring in.
Since when was crafting this entertaining to watch?
As far as Leon was concerned, the competition would mostly involve players sitting in front of their forging tools, hammering away at their anvils, and... well, that's it.
The only interesting part was when the crafting was finally complete.

That was probably why the host always went out of their way to keep things engaging—whether by adding unnecessary drama, discussing random topics, or even outright distracting the participants with unexpected questions to get a reaction from the crowd.
Well, what else could they do?
Forging takes time. A lot of time.

And interestingly, for this Blacksmith Crafting Competition, the time acceleration in the private server was set to match the same speed as the main server of Immortal Legacy. Three times faster than the real world.
And the structure of the event?
Insane.
The competition would last for a full 48 hours, with only 8 hours of rest for every 24-hour cycle—essentially replicating the in-game conditions.
Two days of non-stop forging?
This had to be one of the most time-consuming competitions than the rest.

There were 32 participants in total. Most of them were unfamiliar to Leon, as players from all over the continents had gathered for this event. The only ones he recognized were those who had competed against him in the Dissidia Kingdom.
Once everything was set, each participant entered their respective capsule devices.

As the system activated, Leon found himself transported to a flat platform—a dedicated workspace where a fully equipped blacksmithing station was already set up, customized with tools matching each participant's specialization.
Inside the game, the host stepped forward onto a virtual stage, their voice amplified across the arena.
And with that, they began the official opening of the Blacksmith Competition, laying out the general rules for everyone.
"Welcome, everyone, to the Blacksmith Crafting Competition!
To all our participants, here's what you need to know—
You have complete freedom to craft anything you want. All necessary materials have been provided, so resource gathering won't be an issue.
As for blueprints, you can choose from the pre-approved selection available... or, if you're feeling confident, you're free to use your own blueprint.
Now, let me be clear—how you craft your item doesn't matter. What matters is the final result.
The winner will be determined by the end product, no matter what method, technique, or strategy you use to get there.
But don't forget—this is a race against time. The competition may run for 48 real-time hours, but inside the game, that translates to a total of four full days.
So use your time wisely—every second counts.
And with that—good luck to all participants! Let's see what legends will be forged today!"
The moment the host finished speaking, all participants immediately rushed toward the materials table.

There, stacks of high-quality materials were neatly arranged—ores, enchanted ingots, refined metals, and even Monster Cores and Monster Soul Stones. Among them were rare materials that only a handful of players had ever encountered in the game.

Broken followed the crowd, making his way to the materials stand while observing the others. Each player was carefully inspecting the available resources, already strategizing what they wanted to craft.

The blueprints were also laid out nearby, though the selection was somewhat limited—only 20 armor sets and a dozen or so weapons were available. Still, it was an impressive list, as every single one required an Advanced Rank Blacksmith to forge.
As players hurriedly grabbed their chosen blueprints and materials, Broken exhaled a long sigh.
Looking at all these expensive materials piled up in one place...
If only he could take them back to the actual Immortal Legacy server.
With this kind of resource stockpile, he could forge some of the strongest items in the game. He could even build a powerful golem army without worrying about material shortages.
What a waste...
Still standing there, Broken watched as the other competitors moved quickly, most of them rushing to gather their materials as fast as possible.
Time was everything.
No matter how skilled they were, the fact remained—four days in-game was barely enough to craft smaller items like gloves, boots, or helmets.
But for those aiming to craft weapons—which held far greater value—it was a gamble.
With such a short time frame, every second counted.
Broken remained where he was, watching as more and more blacksmiths finished gathering their materials and left the area.
Among the few remaining, he noticed a familiar face—or at least, a name that seemed vaguely familiar.
Where have I seen him before...?
Before he could place it, the player approached him directly.
"Thinking of cheating your way to victory?" the player sneered.
The name Titonor hovered above his head.
Broken frowned, giving him a blank stare. "What?"
"This is the second time we've been in the same competition," Titonor continued. "And this time, I won't lose."
Broken raised an eyebrow, still trying to remember where he had seen this guy before.
"Uh... sorry, have we met before?" he asked, genuinely confused.
Titonor's expression instantly changed.
For a moment, he looked utterly stunned, as if his brain had short-circuited. His mouth opened slightly, searching for a response, before he finally blurted out—
"I was there when you were at Clario Town's Blacksmith Smithy! And also in the Dissidia Kingdom Competition!"
"Oh," Broken replied casually. Then, with a shrug, he added, "Sorry, too many people there—I don't remember everyone." He flashed a small grin.
Titonor's face twitched. Without another word, the man spun on his heel and walked away... only to suddenly pause, mutter something under his breath, and turn back around.
He grabbed a Monster Core and a Monster Soul Stone from the table before finally stomping off.
Broken remained in place, waiting until the last of the blacksmiths had finished gathering their materials.
That was when another figure approached him. This time, it was a name he definitely recognized. Lanceshot.
"I wonder why your name isn't on the leaderboard," Lanceshot remarked casually.
"Yeah... I didn't register my name," Broken replied simply.
Lanceshot gave a thin smile, his tone dropping into something almost mocking.

"No need to be shy, you know. Maybe if you actually put your name in, the leaderboard would be more interesting... Because honestly? Being the only blacksmith with Expert Rank in Immortal Legacy is getting kinda boring. Maybe you should put in a bit more effort and work your way up there too."
He spoke casually, but the arrogance in his words was impossible to miss.
Broken just smiled. "That's an impressive achievement—being the only Expert-Rank Blacksmith. I mean, I've never even been in Advanced Rank, let alone Expert Rank."
Which was true—he had never been in the Advanced or Expert Rank. Because he had skipped straight from Beginner to Master Rank.
Lanceshot chuckled, clearly taking that as an admission of inferiority.

"Not even Advanced Rank? You surely like to joke around, huh," Lanceshot scoffed. Then, with a confident smirk, he added, "Well then, good luck with the contest. At least try to aim for second place... because first place is definitely mine."
He turned away, walking off with the same self-assured arrogance.
Broken just smiled—calm, unbothered. "Good luck to you too."
Was that all?
Or was there anyone else who wanted to run their mouth at Broken before the competition even started?
Seeing that no one else was approaching him, Broken finally made his move.

Now it was his turn to gather materials. Without hesitation, he walked straight toward the section where the Soul Stones were piled up. There were hundreds of them, waiting to be shaped into something greater.
He reached out.
And took all of them.
