chapters.title: Chapter 793 - The Semifinals Begin!
paragraphs: The Eternal Challenge was steadily reaching its most crucial matches, bringing the overall event closer to its climax. With more highly anticipated battles taking place, the excitement in the air was undeniable. The stadiums were packed to the brim, filled with roaring spectators who could no longer contain their energy—shouting, cheering, and rallying behind their favorite players.

Still on the horizon was the Raid Race Final, set to take place near the end of the event, and of course, the Duel of Champions—the final match that would close the tournament and determine who would claim the title as the first-ever Duel of Champions winner, solidifying their position as the strongest champion of the Eternal Challenge.

On top of that, the Team Battle was shaping up to be an unforgettable spectacle, something that would only fuel the audience's insatiable thirst for more. But this time, everyone's long-awaited dream was about to come true—the chance to witness the top players, who had long been scattered across different continents within the game, brought together on a single battleground for an all-out clash!

Watching players take on monsters had always been thrilling, but nothing could compare to a battle between the very best, set in a well-structured, high-stakes environment. The sheer intensity of it all would surpass anything that had ever been seen in the game before.
The Semifinals Begin!
Early that day, the semifinals of the Duel of Champions were finally about to take place. The first match? Frostedge vs. Akiko—a battle between two Divine Champions.

Frostedge was known as a legendary solo player, a name that carried weight across the entire game. As one of the Pride Champions, he was infamous for possessing an unfathomable number of skills—so many that no one had ever been able to determine the full extent of his abilities. Even now, his Divine Blessing remained a mystery.

Facing him was Akiko, a member of the Horde of Hell Guild and the feared Gluttony Champion. She was known as the most unstoppable assassin, a player who had never let a single target escape alive. With her demonic appearance—a pair of wings and menacing horns—she was as terrifying as her reputation suggested.
Both were close-range fighters—a battle of sword magic vs. dual blades. This was a match that no one would want to miss.
Meanwhile, in the other semifinal, it was Broken vs. Elincia.

Speculation about Broken being a Divine Champion had been circulating for some time, but what truly shocked people was that he was originally known as a blacksmith—yet had proven himself to be an exceptional fighter, both in-game and in this tournament.
His opponent? Elincia. The strongest mage in Immortal Legacy.

What made this battle even more interesting was their shared history—Elincia was the former leader of the Ass Guild, a small yet elite guild known for its high achievements and powerhouse members. Eventually, that guild was absorbed into a new guild, formed and now led by none other than Broken himself.
So, this match wasn't just about victory.
It was a battle between a former guild leader and the current guild leader!
How would this rivalry unfold?
The world would find out today!

As the two contestants stepped onto the stage, the crowd erupted into cheers. Han Feng and the player behind Akiko had arrived, and the host wasted no time in making the moment even more electrifying.

Han Feng, already well known among the audience, sat in his wheelchair with someone standing behind him, accompanying him. Meanwhile, Akiko, a young woman in her early twenties, had a distinct Japanese appearance, her expression calm yet determined.
The host turned to Akiko first.

"It is an honor to stand on this stage today," Akiko said with a graceful bow, her voice polite yet unwavering. "But do not mistake my respect for hesitation—when the battle begins, I will fight with everything I have."
The crowd roared in approval as the host then shifted the focus to Han Feng.

Han Feng gave a small nod before responding, his tone humble yet firm. "The honor is mine as well. Facing a warrior like you is something I will not take lightly. No matter the outcome, I look forward to giving my all in this match."

The stadium erupted once more, the energy reaching new heights. It was clear that national pride was running high—China vs. Japan. The clash between these two top players was already fueling intense excitement among the spectators.
With formalities complete, both contestants entered their capsule devices, and within seconds, their in-game avatars appeared in stunning detail on the massive screen at the center of the stadium.
The battle was about to begin!

As a Gluttony Champion, Akiko's Blessing remained largely a mystery. She was infamous for being completely unaffected by any attack that hit her. It was as if she could simply nullify incoming strikes, making her one of the most feared assassins in the game.
What made her even deadlier was her incredible mobility—she could fly. The combination of flight and her ability to nullify attacks made her an absolute nightmare to deal with in battle.

However, during her previous fight against Elincia and Ivana, her Blessing had finally been exposed. It was Fokil who had managed to take her down in one strike—by hurling a hammer at her from extreme range.
This led to an important discovery:
Akiko's Blessing allowed her to nullify all incoming attacks—or rather, projectile attacks—but only if they were launched from within a certain distance.
This meant that long-range attacks that exceeded the threshold of her Blessing's effect could still hit her.
And Frostedge knew this.

He had been there when that battle took place—watching from the same carriage as Broken, Freya, and the others. He had seen Fokil's attack land the finishing blow, meaning he had likely already formulated a plan to take her down.
However... Akiko's biggest threat wasn't just her Blessing.
It was her mobility.
With her high-speed flight, she could weave through attacks with ease, making it nearly impossible for a close-combat fighter like Frostedge to land a solid hit.

His magic attacks were effective at mid-range, but they weren't nearly as devastating as his full-power melee strikes. Against an opponent like Akiko, who could stay airborne and evade attacks effortlessly, this would be an incredibly difficult fight.
This was a major battle, and most people had placed their bets on Frostedge to win. However, what stood out was that the betting margin wasn't that large.
This alone proved that Akiko was not an opponent to be underestimated.
She had reached this stage of the tournament with a perfect record—winning every single match without losing a single point of health. Every victory had been flawless.
Meanwhile, for Leon and Euna, this match was particularly significant—it would determine who they might face in the final match, should they advance past their own semifinal.
"Frostedge can't afford to hold back anymore, can he?" Euna asked as she sat with Leon and Maylon, as usual.
"I hope not," Maylon replied. "Because if he keeps holding back, I'm not sure it'll be enough to get him to the final match."
After a brief pause, Maylon added, "Let's see what kind of abilities we can uncover from his Blessing in this fight."
Understanding an opponent's strengths and weaknesses was the key to victory.
And this battle? It was going to be the ultimate revelation.

chapters.title: Chapter 794 - Not a Single Hit—Yet
paragraphs: The entire stadium locked its attention onto the massive screen as the countdown hit zero.
Finally—the long-awaited battle between Frostedge and Akiko had begun!

Since both were close-combat fighters, neither hesitated. The moment the match started, they dashed toward each other, closing the gap in an instant. And what followed was nothing short of breathtaking.

It was simply amazing—the sheer precision of their movements, the flawless swordplay, the way they clashed with perfect timing. Every strike was met with a parry, every opening was exploited and countered, and every step was executed with an almost inhuman level of finesse.

The exchange was so fluid and intense that it felt like watching a choreographed masterpiece—except this was a real battle, where both fighters were constantly seeking that one decisive hit to deal massive damage.
Leon, watching with wide eyes, couldn't help but be in awe.
Even before they had unleashed any powerful spells or abilities, their sheer technical skill was already on full display.
"Both of them are insanely skilled with the sword," Euna was the first to comment beside Leon.
"Yeah, too many people are good with swords," Leon muttered.
"You're not bad yourself, huh?" she smirked. "You've been making solid progress with your spear these past few months."
Leon didn't respond, his focus still locked onto the battle.
One thing was clear—at this stage of the fight, neither of them had landed a clean hit.
A glance at their Health Points confirmed it.
Akiko had taken zero damage—as expected. Her Blessing ensured that she was untouched so far.
Frostedge, on the other hand, had also parried every attack flawlessly—his health remained completely intact.
But that was exactly why this wasn't looking good for him.
"If Frostedge keeps holding back, this fight won't end in his favor," Maylon commented.
"I think he needs to drop the act and start using his skills," Euna added, turning toward Maylon.
"That's exactly what needs to happen," Maylon agreed.

Akiko fully utilized her mobility with her wings, soaring, dashing, and striking with her twin swords at incredible speed. Meanwhile, Frostedge glided across the ice beneath his feet, delivering attacks that were not only precise and powerful but also breathtakingly graceful.
From a distance, it almost didn't look like a fight—it looked like a beautifully choreographed dance.
Like, seriously.
Akiko swept through the air elegantly, her wings carrying her as she spun mid-flight, slicing, diving, evading, and striking again in a flawless rhythm.

Meanwhile, Frostedge skated effortlessly across the ice, his movements fluid and untouchable. Each time Akiko attacked, he slid backward just enough to avoid the hit—but instead of losing momentum, he would twist his body and launch himself forward again, like he had built-in boosters on his feet.
Then, in a dramatic moment, Frostedge leaped into the air—his sword clashing against Akiko's in a mid-air battle that sent both of them flying backward.
Yet, even after all that—neither had taken a single hit.

The entire audience was stunned. The sheer elegance and precision of their fight made it feel less like a battle and more like a live martial arts performance, showcasing just how vast the gap was between normal players and those at the absolute top.
They weren't just strong—they were untouchable.
And of course, the audience couldn't hold back their reactions:
"Bro, I can't even dodge a fireball properly, and these two are out here playing aerial chess with swords."
"If I tried to fight like this, I'd trip over my own feet and die instantly."
"They're not even hitting each other, and somehow this is still the most insane fight I've ever seen."
"Plot twist: The real battle is who can look cooler while dodging."
"At this point, just give them a soundtrack and a slow-motion camera, and we got ourselves an Oscar-winning action movie."
As the fight continued, even though it had only been a minute, it was clear that neither side would win at this rate.
Akiko remained untouched, while Frostedge expertly wielded his sword, matching her movements perfectly.
They needed a decisive strike—something that could actually end this battle.
Euna spoke up. "Frostedge wouldn't step into this match without some kind of plan, right?"
Maylon immediately responded. "I have to admit, he's a genius, so yeah, I'm sure he has something up his sleeve."

"Damn, now I'm curious... Why is he still engaging in close combat like this? It's obvious that Akiko dominates in speed, while Frostedge's true strength lies in his magic sword fighting. He needs to cast his spells.
Leon nodded slightly, following their conversation, and at that exact moment—on the massive screen in the stadium—things finally started to change.
Frostedge stopped playing Akiko's game.
Finally, he cast his spells.
A massive ice shard materialized in midair and came crashing down onto the battlefield.
But with her insane speed, Akiko easily dodged it—the shard slammed into the ground, standing tall like a frozen monument at the center of the arena.
Frostedge didn't stop. He kept evading her attacks, all while summoning more ice shards, each one embedding itself deep into the battlefield like enormous icy pillars.
Euna frowned. "What is Frostedge doing? With shards that huge, there's no way he can hit Akiko."
Maylon smirked slightly. "I think he's finally showing his ability. He's not casting them to hit her."

Euna replied again, "But still, if Frostedge wants to win, he has to land a hit on Akiko from a distance. And yeah, speaking as someone who's fought her before, that's easier said than done—even with my ability to fly. It's going to be even harder for Frostedge, who relies on his sword to stay airborne."
Meanwhile, over at the caster's desk, Brando and Paul were deep in discussion, their voices charged with excitement as they analyzed the battle.

Brando spoke first, his tone filled with energy. "Alright, everyone, we're seeing something interesting happening here! Frostedge is finally using his magic, but—hold on—he's not even trying to hit Akiko?! Those massive ice shards keep slamming into the ground instead of their target! What is he thinking?!"

Paul responded immediately. "At a glance, it looks like Frostedge is just wasting his spells, because we all know Akiko's mobility is off the charts—she can dodge anything thrown at her. But here's the problem—Frostedge can't afford to play her game forever. If he doesn't take control of the battlefield, he's going to lose."
Brando let out a breath, shaking his head. "Man, what is Frostedge planning?! He's got to make a move soon, or this fight is slipping through his fingers!"

On the massive screen, it was clear—Akiko, with her blinding speed, kept weaving through the falling ice shards with ease. Not a single one touched her as she danced through the air, effortlessly avoiding every attack.
And then, for the first time in the match, she managed to land a clean hit.

Spinning at high velocity, she struck Frostedge with a powerful mid-air slash, sending him flying backward. He barely managed to block with his sword, but the sheer force of her attack sent him crashing hard across the battlefield.
For the first time, Frostedge took damage!
His health bar visibly dropped, and the crowd erupted in shock and excitement.
Akiko was closing in on victory. Seeing her opponent finally weakened, she didn't hesitate—she kept pressing forward, determined to end the match.

The entire stadium was on fire. Fans from both sides, representing the two dominant nations, were on their feet, cheering wildly, their voices merging into a deafening roar of support for their respective champions.

chapters.title: Chapter 795 - Reflections of a Champion
paragraphs: The entire audience was on the edge of their seats, eyes locked onto the screen, completely absorbed in the cat-and-mouse game unfolding before them.
Frostedge had littered the battlefield with massive ice shards, seemingly using them as cover to escape from Akiko, whose speed and relentless pursuit made it nearly impossible for him to fight back.
At least, that's what everyone thought.
How could they not? Up to this point, Frostedge had yet to land a single meaningful hit.

Meanwhile, Akiko remained untouched, her health still at full. She was darting effortlessly between the towering ice formations, closing in on Frostedge again and again, delivering sharp, precise strikes that kept chipping away at his health.
By now, Frostedge had already lost nearly half his HP.
At this rate, it seemed obvious who was going to win.
"No way Akiko's actually going to win this, right?" Euna muttered, watching the fight intently.
But beside her, Maylon simply shook his head. "No. Frostedge is going to win this."
Euna raised an eyebrow at his answer.

Even the casters and commentators had already started setting the narrative—Akiko was moments away from delivering the finishing blow. The battle looked like it was reaching its inevitable conclusion, with Frostedge barely hanging on.
But then again... whatever Frostedge was doing, it was clear that he was building toward something.
Yet, despite all the spells he had cast, despite all the ice shards he had dropped onto the battlefield, not a single attack had landed on Akiko.
Not even once.
At that moment, Akiko suddenly stopped chasing.
The entire stadium held its breath.
On the massive screen, the camera zoomed in on Akiko's confused expression—her sharp, focused gaze wavering for the first time.
Because all around her, the battlefield had changed.
The towering ice shards Frostedge had been summoning all this time had transformed the arena into a massive hall of mirrors.
Reflections of Frostedge appeared everywhere.
Brando said with enthusiasm, his voice rising into a near shout.
"Wait, what?! What just happened?! Akiko looks confused—"
"No way... NO WAY! Look at this! The ice shards! Frostedge wasn't trying to hit Akiko at all—he was building a goddamn mirror maze!"
"That's insane! This entire time, he wasn't running away—he was setting the stage! Akiko can't tell which reflection is real!"
The audience erupted, realizing what Frostedge had been planning all along. He hadn't been running—he had been hiding in plain sight.
For the first time, Akiko hesitated.
Realizing she was wasting time chasing illusions, she immediately took to the skies, believing she could spot the real Frostedge from above. But that was where she made her mistake.
The moment she soared higher, something changed. Her Blessing's range—the distance at which she could nullify attacks—was now no longer in effect.
From below, small ice shards suddenly shot up toward her.
She reacted quickly, twisting her body mid-air to dodge—but one of them clipped her.
For the first time, Akiko took damage. Her health bar finally dropped.
The entire stadium gasped in shock.
"OH MY GOD! Akiko's been HIT! THAT'S DAMAGE! THAT'S ACTUAL DAMAGE!"
"This is GENIUS! This entire fight, he wasn't playing her game—he was leading her exactly where he wanted her to be!"
The crowd went wild.
Frostedge's plan was now crystal clear. By creating the mirror maze, he had forced Akiko to waste time searching for him.
And the moment she left the ground, she became exposed. For the first time in the match, Akiko was vulnerable. And Frostedge was about to take full advantage of it.
Leon couldn't help but smile as he watched the scene unfold. He hadn't expected Frostedge to pull off something this wild.
"Damn, this guy is dangerous," Euna muttered.
"Yes, and the match is already over," Maylon added, his voice calm yet certain.

At that moment, Akiko, clearly frustrated, locked her gaze on what she believed was the real Frostedge standing below. Without hesitation, she dove back into the mirror maze, determined to land a decisive hit.
But the moment she reentered the icy battlefield—a massive explosion erupted.
The entire arena shook as a chain reaction of detonations ignited around her. The ice shards Frostedge had planted earlier weren't just mirrors—they were traps.
The screen flickered and shook, struggling to capture what was happening as a series of relentless icy blasts engulfed Akiko's last known position.
Then—after a long moment of chaos—
Her profile on the screen turned red.
Match over.
And when the battlefield finally cleared, only one figure remained standing amid the rapidly melting ice.
Frostedge.
The stadium erupted. The crowd roared. The casters lost their minds.
Brando practically shouted into his mic. "HOLY—THAT'S IT! FROSTEDGE WINS! FROSTEDGE WINS! WHAT DID WE JUST WITNESS?!"
Paul's voice cut in, full of admiration. "That wasn't just a fight—that was a masterpiece. Frostedge turned the battlefield itself into his weapon!"
Brando's excitement was off the charts. "HE LURED HER IN, SET THE STAGE, AND THEN BAM! FINISHED HER IN ONE CLEAN SWEEP! THIS WASN'T JUST A WIN—THIS WAS A STATEMENT!"
Paul nodded. "Akiko was undefeated up until now, but Frostedge just proved why he's in the absolute top tier of players. This wasn't just about power—it was pure strategy."
Brando let out a breath, still buzzing with energy. "And just like that, Frostedge moves on to the final match! What a fight! What a moment! I CAN'T WAIT TO SEE WHAT HAPPENS NEXT!
The cheers didn't stop. The stadium was electric.
Frostedge had won—and he had done it in spectacular fashion.
Leon let out a deep breath as he watched the battle conclude.
What a worthy opponent to face in the final.
And now, it was set in stone—he would be there, standing against this man, against his brilliance, his genius. And he was determined to win.
But before any of that could happen, he and everyone else knew exactly what stood in his way.
Beside him, Euna nudged his shoulder with a smirk. "Let's go, champion. You're still planning to settle your unfinished business, right? Elincia's ready to crush you all over again." She giggled.
Leon glanced at her, his eyes sharp with resolve. "Just so you know—I'm not holding back this time."
And just as the cheers from Frostedge and Akiko's battle finally began to settle, Leon and Euna stepped down from the stands, making their way toward the stage.
The moment they moved, the cameras locked onto them.
Their faces flashed across the massive screen.
And just like that, the crowd roared to life once more.
The excitement wasn't over—not even close.
The host wasted no time hyping up the moment.
"OH-HO! LOOK WHO'S UP NEXT! LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, OUR NEXT CONTENDERS HAVE ARRIVED!"
"AFTER THAT UNBELIEVABLE MATCH, DO YOU THINK WE'RE DONE?! NO WAY!"
"BECAUSE NOW—IT'S TIME FOR ANOTHER HIGH-STAKES SHOWDOWN!"
"IT'S A BATTLE OF LEGENDS—A CLASH BETWEEN PAST AND PRESENT—TWO TITANS READY TO SETTLE THE SCORE!"
"WHO WILL CLAIM VICTORY?! WHO WILL MOVE ON TO THE FINAL?! LET'S FIND OUT—RIGHT NOW!"
The crowd erupted once more.
The stage was set.
And the battle?
About to begin.

[Jacob_Weinberg_2081]: "Somewhere in the background, Frostedge is watching like, 'Hurry up, I got a final to win.'"
[DaoistzsPGef]: "WHO CARES WHO WINS, JUST GIVE US A GOOD FIGHT!"
[Lucas_Stellabotte]: "Elincia's literally that one senior employee who left, and now she's back to show the new guy who's REALLY in charge."

chapters.title: Chapter 796: Storm vs. Spear
paragraphs: The stage was set.

On the massive screen, the figures of Broken and Elincia appeared, their avatars highlighted from a dramatic overhead shot before the camera zoomed in to capture their faces. The countdown timer had already begun, ticking down from 10.
The crowd was electric—cheers, chants, and roars of excitement filled the stadium.

Elincia's face appeared crystal clear on the screen, and the reaction was immediate. Despite the fact that in-game appearances were usually enhanced, Elincia's beauty in Immortal Legacy was eerily close to her real-life self—flawless, without a single imperfection.
From across the battlefield, her voice rang out, carrying a teasing edge. "Use your summons, and I'm sure you'll win easily."
A loud "Woooo!" erupted from the audience at her playful taunt.
"Because if you hold back, I doubt you'll stand a chance against me, huh?"
Broken smirked slightly. "You think I'd lose just because I don't use my summons?"
"I've already warned you," Elincia replied as crackling lightning began to surge around her form.

Broken chuckled. "Then you should use the Spellweaver Chrono Booster—that way, you can cast your ridiculous skills even faster and try to finish me off right away." His grin widened slightly. "I wouldn't mind if you used it to try and take me down."

Elincia smirked back. "Oh? Are you saying I'd lose without that borrowed item of yours?" She flipped her hair back confidently. "No need to worry—I'll still give you an amazing performance without it, Broken."
The crowd erupted, completely eating up the interaction.
These weren't just two top players going head-to-head. They had history.

Everyone knew how close Broken and Elincia were—how they were often seen sitting together during matches, how their past guilds were intertwined, and of course, the infamous merging of the Ass Guild into Vensalor Guild.
This match wasn't just about who was stronger.
This was Ex-Guild Leader vs. Current Guild Leader.
This was a battle that HAD to happen.
The countdown hit 0.
The match began!
A rippling wave of cheers and shouts echoed across the entire stadium the moment Elincia's body lifted into the air.
Her flowing blue robe blended with the crackling blue lightning that surged violently around her, illuminating the battlefield in a breathtaking display of raw magical energy.

On the other side, Broken had already drawn his spear—his signature weapon, the one he always relied on in battle. His stance shifted into an offensive position, fully prepared to counter whatever came next.
Broken knew exactly what Elincia was doing.

There was no way she would use the Spellweaver Chrono Booster. Even though that item allowed her to cast any spell instantly, Broken had too many defensive measures that would make those 10 seconds of advantage completely useless.
Not to mention, Elincia's mana consumption would be massive if she relied on that strategy. Instead, she would likely focus on utility spells—ones that could strip Broken of his protective defenses.
And just as he predicted, she made her move.
Elincia's body suddenly blurred as she darted left and right at impossible speeds.
Then—
Something insane happened.
Elincia's body split apart.
In a flash, multiple copies of her burst outward in every direction, each one still crackling with lightning, their forms encircling Broken from all angles.
The crowd erupted in gasps and cheers at the stunning sight.
Without hesitation, each Elincia fired off rapid bursts of lightning, bombarding Broken from all sides with relentless pew-pew energy blasts.
Broken immediately took off running, dodging the incoming attacks, leaping into the air, and thrusting his spear toward one of the Elincia copies.
His attack landed—but the moment his spear struck, her body simply vanished.
A phantom.
Not real.
At the same time, Elincia recalled something Maylon had said before—an analysis of Broken's Invincible Paragon ability.
His defensive skill set was absurdly layered. Most notably, his Invincible Shields provided 12 layers of protection, meaning he could nullify up to 12 attacks before taking any real damage.

That was why her strategy was simple—strip those shields away first. By continuously bombarding him with small, rapid attacks, she could chip away at his defenses—until he had nothing left to protect himself.

The early phase of the fight looked almost one-sided—Elincia appeared to be toying with Broken, continuously attacking from all directions with her illusion skills, while Broken kept dashing, weaving, and lunging with his spear, desperately trying to land a hit.
But every time he struck—nothing. Just another illusion fading into thin air.
At this rate, it was clear that Broken, as a close-range fighter, would simply be kited to death if Elincia kept her distance, flying above him while bombarding him from afar.
He had to do something.

Maylon had already broken it down for Elincia before the match. "Once his 12 layers of Invincible Shield are gone, the next thing protecting him is a massive chunk of Earth-based Health Shield. Your lightning attacks are highly effective against it. So when the time comes, go all in with a high-damage lightning strike."
And just like that—the moment Broken failed to land even a single hit—Elincia raised both hands above her head.
Immediately, the arena shook violently.
A deep, thunderous rumble filled the stadium, growing louder by the second. The screen flashed white for a split moment before—
A barrage of massive lightning strikes came crashing down.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
The ground exploded with blinding energy, each impact ripping through the battlefield as Elincia unleashed her full power.
Broken barely had a moment to react. He activated Invincible Force Reflection, a skill that allowed him to reflect all incoming damage for exactly two seconds.
But—
Elincia's attack lasted longer than two seconds.
The continuous bombardment outlasted his defense, striking him directly after his reflection effect wore off.
And because Elincia remained at a safe distance, there was no way for him to counterattack.
When the lightning storm finally subsided, the dust settled, revealing Broken still standing in the center of the arena.

And now—it was truly about to begin.

Elincia smirked back.
"Oh?

Instead, she would likely focus on utility spells—ones that could strip Broken of his protective defenses.

Elincia's body suddenly blurred as she darted left and right at impossible speeds.

Something insane happened.
Elincia's body split apart.
In a flash, multiple copies of her burst outward in every direction, each one still crackling with lightning, their forms encircling Broken from all angles.

chapters.title: Chapter 797: Storm vs. Sea
paragraphs: Broken needed to clear out Elincia's clones—something he couldn't do with melee attacks alone. His spear, while powerful, wasn't exactly ideal against a mage who had both high mobility and flight advantage.
However...
His Mythic-grade Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear wasn't just any weapon. It wasn't just for close-range combat. This spear had an arsenal of AOE attacks.
[🌪️ Abyssal Cascade - Torrent of Destruction (Active Skill) activated]
The moment Broken cast the skill, a violent surge of water erupted around him, twisting into a tornado of destructive force.
The massive torrent sucked in everything nearby, the sheer pressure making it impossible to escape.
Elincia's clones, despite their speed, were dragged mercilessly into the raging vortex, their forms dissolving one by one as they were shredded apart by the force.
The stadium erupted in deafening cheers as the screen showed the spectacle—Broken turning the tide in a single move!
But—
There was still one Elincia left.
The real one.
And she had already soared far above the battlefield.
Broken's gaze locked onto her—he could see her clearly.
Then—
A flash.
A massive explosion of light.
The sky darkened, heavy storm clouds rolling in as if a natural disaster was unfolding.
And then—
Lightning rained down.
The entire arena became a storming warzone, crackling bolts of energy striking the battlefield in rapid succession.
Lightning Field.
One of Elincia's most dangerous abilities. A high-level area skill that not only boosted all her lightning-based attacks but also gave her even greater speed and mobility.
Broken was trapped.
The entire battlefield had become her domain.
From her position high above, Elincia could strike freely.
And Broken? He was stuck inside the storm.
Brando practically lost it the moment the battlefield transformed into a storm of destruction.
"HOLY—ARE YOU SEEING THIS?! ELINCIA JUST TURNED THE ENTIRE ARENA INTO A LIGHTNING HELL!!"
His voice boomed across the stadium as the crowd erupted in wild cheers.
"LOOK AT THIS!! BROKEN JUST WIPED OUT HER CLONES—BUT GUESS WHAT?! ELINCIA WAS ALREADY TEN STEPS AHEAD!!"
The screen flashed with blinding streaks of lightning, the battlefield now an unstoppable death zone.
"AND NOW—BROKEN IS STUCK! HE CAN'T ESCAPE! HE CAN'T FIGHT BACK!"
Brando threw his hands up in pure excitement.
"THIS IS INSANE! SHE'S NOT JUST FIGHTING—SHE'S CONTROLLING THE ENTIRE DAMN BATTLEFIELD!!"
The energy in the stadium reached an explosive high.
Lightning crashed down, and all eyes were locked on Broken.
Would he survive the storm? Or was this the end?!
The lightning strikes were undeniably powerful, but they weren't continuous. Each bolt struck in intervals, meaning that as long as Broken kept moving, he could avoid being hit.
And in that moment—
He switched his armor. His entire gear shifted, and suddenly, he wasn't a spear-wielding warrior anymore.
[Woodland Ranger Armor Equipped]
"Oh, so now he's an archer?"
Without wasting a second, Broken pulled out his Golden Bow of Artemis and immediately dashed across the battlefield, weaving between the explosive lightning impacts with remarkable agility.
He drew his bow, took aim, and fired—
Arrow after arrow shot toward the sky, streaking toward Elincia, turning this into a full-blown ranged battle—Mage vs. Archer!
Elincia, still in the air, moved with incredible speed, dodging every single arrow, her body almost blurring as she shifted directions.
But at the same time—Broken was dodging her lightning.
It was a battle of reflexes, timing, and precision.
Then—the moment everything changed.
Broken switched his strategy again.
His spear reappeared in his hands—but instead of using it for melee combat, he loaded it into his bow.
The entire stadium held its breath.
Broken drew back the bowstring, the massive spear glowing with immense energy.
The sky split open.
A colossal spear manifested above the battlefield.
And then—
Broken let it loose. At that exact moment, the storm above clashed violently with the ocean-like energy building around him.
Lightning met water.
The arena exploded into chaos as lightning and a massive sea-like torrent collided in a destructive wave that tore through the battlefield!
It was pure chaos wrapped in beauty—a stunning display of skill that left everyone breathless.
Who would have thought?
These two key figures of Vensalor Guild, clashing at such an insane level, their battle elevated by the massive arena screen, the booming sound effects, and the sheer intensity of their abilities.
This wasn't just a fight. This was an event worth witnessing.
Broken didn't let up.
The moment his spear attack concluded, he immediately switched weapons again.
[Bedrock Breaker Equipped.]
Massive boulders began raining from the sky, crashing down alongside the still-raging lightning field, the two elements mixing into a spectacle of destruction.
And then—
A pickaxe, shot toward Elincia, launching directly at her airborne form.
For the first time, she couldn't avoid it. The moment the attack connected, her body lurched mid-air, throwing off her balance.
That was all the opening Broken needed. He fired arrows relentlessly, his shots precise and unyielding, striking at her continuously.
The Lightning Field that had once trapped him?
Now? It was as if it didn't affect him at all.
At that moment, Elincia finally crashed to the ground, her body now enveloped in a protective barrier sphere.
Broken didn't stop. He rushed forward, continuously firing arrows, his attacks relentless yet precise.
And despite the intensity of the battle, despite the high stakes, it was clear—
They were both enjoying this.
Every attack, every counter, every second of this fight—Broken was having the time of his life.
Brando practically exploded with excitement.
"ARE YOU SEEING THIS?!! ELINCIA—A PLAYER WITH NO DIVINE BLESSING, NO HIGH-GRADE CLASS—JUST GAVE BROKEN ONE OF THE TOUGHEST FIGHTS OF HIS LIFE!!"
His voice boomed across the stadium, the energy of the crowd surging even higher.
"THIS IS WHAT TRUE SKILL LOOKS LIKE! PURE TALENT, STRATEGY, AND EXECUTION!"
He barely caught his breath before shouting again.
"AND BROKEN—LOOK AT HIM! HE'S NOT JUST FIGHTING TO WIN—HE'S LOVING EVERY SECOND OF THIS!!
"If it wasn't Elincia, the talented mage of Immortal Legacy, then no one could have pulled off something like this."
Paul, his analytical side still intact, chimed in with a knowing edge.
"Because this isn't just a battle, Brando. This is a moment. A moment where two of the best players in Immortal Legacy are going all out, showing the world what peak-level play truly looks like."
Brando's voice rose one last time.
"LEGENDARY. THIS MATCH IS ALREADY LEGENDARY!!"
And the crowd?
Absolutely lost their minds.
The battle continued for a few more moments, the tension still lingering—until, finally, the Lightning Field dissipated.
When the dust settled, Broken stood right in front of Elincia.
His spear had pierced through her chest.
Her health plummeted instantly.
The two of them locked eyes, both still catching their breath, but their expressions weren't those of frustration or regret.
They were smiling. They had enjoyed every second of this battle.
Elincia let out a soft chuckle. "Thanks for the unforgettable battle, Guild Leader."
Broken gave a small nod, his tone filled with genuine respect. "Thanks for your guidance and humility all this time."
And then—
The stadium erupted.
A thunderous roar of applause and cheers filled the entire arena, the crowd losing themselves in the moment.
Yes, Broken had won.
But that wasn't what mattered most.
What mattered was this battle.
A fight so beautiful, so intense, so perfect, it was something that might never happen again.
This was a match to be remembered.
Brando's voice exploded through the speakers, his energy completely off the charts.
"WHAT. A. MATCH!! I DON'T CARE WHO WON OR LOST—THIS WAS PURE PERFECTION!!"
He barely took a breath before continuing.
"TWO LEGENDS, TWO TITANS—AND THEY GAVE US ONE OF THE GREATEST FIGHTS IN THE HISTORY OF IMMORTAL LEGACY!!"
The crowd only got louder, feeding off his words.
"AND LOOK AT THEM! THIS WASN'T JUST A COMPETITION—THIS WAS A DUEL BETWEEN COMRADES, BETWEEN TWO MASTERS OF THEIR CRAFT!!"
Paul said. "There are moments in gaming history that stand the test of time... and this? This is one of them."
Brando didn't even try to hold back his excitement.
"BROKEN WINS! BUT ELINCIA?! SHE LEAVES THIS STAGE AS A LEGEND!!"
The cheers never stopped.
This battle was etched into history.
In the stands, Maylon leaned back, a small smile on his face as he watched the aftermath of the match unfold.
Seated beside him, London glanced over and smirked. "Not bad, huh?"
"Yeah..." Maylon exhaled, his expression calm but amused. "To be honest, we already knew who was going to win. Broken is just... broken."
London let out a short laugh. "Well, the most important thing is that everyone was entertained. And this fight? More than delivered."
Maylon nodded slowly. "Now, the real battle is about to begin in the final."
London's smirk grew as he folded his arms. "Two protagonists going head-to-head... let's see who's the better one. I'm almost convinced this whole thing is scripted."

And this fight?
More than delivered."
Maylon nodded slowly.
"Now, the real battle is about to begin in the final."
London's smirk grew as he folded his arms.
"Two protagonists going head-to-head... let's see who's the better one.
I'm almost convinced this whole thing is scripted."

chapters.title: Chapter 798: They’re Not Alone
paragraphs: What an incredible performance. In the end, Broken emerged victorious against Elincia.

It had been a tricky fight, no doubt—Elincia knew a lot about his combat style and had even discussed strategies with Maylock beforehand to figure out ways to make things as difficult as possible for him.
Broken had secured his spot in the grand final against Frostedge, the ultimate showdown and the final battle of the Eternal Challenge Competition. This was the match everyone had been waiting for.

On one side, Broken had demonstrated incredible versatility and potential, proving himself to be a combat powerhouse throughout the tournament. On the other, Frostedge had yet to reveal anything truly extraordinary. He had fought—and won—every match without ever showing his full strength. It was almost like he had been intentionally holding something back, though no one knew why.

People knew him. They had seen him fight in the game. And the craziest part? Broken and Frostedge had once fought side by side, taking on Galactron together. They had also stood together in the war at Dissidia, but now, they would stand against each other.
This was it—the Grand Final of the Duel of Champions. A battle between two of the strongest contenders in Immortal Legacy.
That day, Hazel contacted Leon with something unexpected.
She had found a group of players exploring the same forest area they had been venturing through in the game.
Who were they?
Curious, Leon decided to log in. Back inside Immortal Legacy.
It was already nighttime in the forest.

The moment Broken set foot into the dense woodland, his sharp eyes quickly noticed SexyGrill standing nearby, partially hidden under the moonlit shadows. As soon as she saw him, she waved enthusiastically before jogging over with her usual energetic demeanor.
"Hi! You won against Elincia, right? That was a great match!" she said, her voice full of excitement.
"Thanks, Grill." Broken nodded, then frowned slightly. "What was it you said earlier?"
SexyGrill's expression turned more serious. "So, there's a group of players, about forty of them."
Broken had already shared access to his flying golem with SexyGrill, allowing them to take turns using it depending on who was logged into the game.
"Forty?" Broken raised an eyebrow. "That's a lot. They're nearby?"
She nodded repeatedly. "Yeah, not far from here. I don't know what they're doing, but their levels are all above 200."
"That's not normal." Broken's voice turned sharp.

Indeed, a group of forty high-level players wandering this deep into the forest wasn't something you'd expect. Then again, what was even more abnormal was that only two players—one of whom wasn't even level 200—were roaming around on their own.
"Yup... I think they're looking for something around here," SexyGrill replied.
Broken nodded slowly.
"Pawpaw, I have a job for you.
Nearby, despite the darkness, a pair of glowing eyes flickered into view—Pawpaw.
He narrowed his eyes at Broken, clearly unimpressed. "What do you want?" he asked with his usual irritated tone.
"Scouting." Broken kept it simple.
Pawpaw said nothing, but without hesitation, his figure vanished into the shadows, disappearing completely as he darted into the darkness.

Broken and SexyGrill had already spent about three weeks in this forest—or at least close to it. Their progress had been slower than expected, mostly because they had to sync their schedules, and Broken was also busy with his matches in the Eternal Challenge, while SexyGrill had to balance her time with school.

Now, they had ventured even deeper into the mountainous region, where the monsters roaming around were at least level 220. That wasn't a small number, especially when dealing with groups of them at once.
Forget local NPCs venturing this far—they hadn't even encountered a single player until now.

Even Broken and SexyGrill had adjusted their exploration strategy in this area, choosing to avoid combat whenever possible. The problem wasn't fighting a single monster—it was that once a battle started, it never seemed to end. More monsters would be drawn in, and before they knew it, they'd be stuck in a nonstop battle loop.
So why were these forty players here?

Were they hunting? No, that didn't make sense. The outer forest had just as many monsters, but they were easier to manage and had similar spawn rates—there was no reason to grind this deep into the wilderness.
That was why this whole thing was so suspicious.
A group of forty high-level players, all gathered here in the middle of nowhere—
Yeah, that was definitely something worth investigating.
After some time, Pawpaw finally discovered something. Without wasting a moment, Broken activated Shared Senses skill, allowing him to see through Pawpaw's eyes.
The demon cat perched silently on a tree branch, gazing down at the scene below.
And there they were—the players.
There were dozens of them, a full-sized party with tankers, frontliners, and support players. Some were leaning against trees, others were eating, and a few were simply chatting with one another.
They were deliberately keeping themselves hidden in the darkness, knowing that any light source could attract monsters.
Broken focused, hoping to catch any useful conversation that might give them a clue. Most of what he heard, however, was just grumbling.
"Hua... I'm so exhausted, and I'm sick of this damn forest."
"We're getting deeper. It won't be much longer now."
"Like hell, we've already been here for two months. Damn it."
"Would you stop complaining? We don't have a choice—we have to complete this mission.
Broken, still observing, turned his attention to SexyGrill and whispered, "Any chance you recognize them? You're from the West Continent—maybe they're from there too?"
SexyGrill furrowed her brows. "No... I don't know them. Maybe they're from a different city than mine... but I have no clue who they are."
For some reason, Broken couldn't shake off the suspicion that these players were somehow connected to the dragonkin. Was he just overthinking it?
Or rather—what if they weren't connected to the dragonkin, but instead... were here to hunt them?
After all, dragonkin were an extremely rare race, with a long and complex history that made them a prime target for those seeking power, knowledge, or something more.
And if they really were searching for the dragonkin...
Then why?
Could they be working under the High Elf Queen?
Broken knew he might be jumping too far ahead, but one thing was certain—he couldn't just let these players wander freely without knowing their true intentions.
For now, the best course of action was to stay close—not too close, but just near enough to observe them and uncover their purpose.
Besides, it wasn't like they had found the dragonkin yet either. If these players were still wandering around, then they were likely just as lost as he was.
"What do you think they're looking for, Grill?"
SexyGrill crossed her arms, her tone playful yet sharp. "Let me take a wild guess... they're after the dragon princess too?"
Broken's gaze hardened slightly. If that were true, then his earlier suspicion wasn't just a stretch—it was a real possibility.
"If they're looking for Ivana... that means they're connected to the High Elf Queen."
"Yeah," SexyGrill nodded. "Because clearly, we're not the only ones who thought Ivana might come here."

He gave a slow nod. "For now, let's stick to them. Stay close, gather information... and make sure they don't detect us. If they see us as a threat, their numbers alone will make them a major problem."
But—
Just as Broken was about to release his shared sense skill with Pawpaw, the demon cat suddenly tensed.
His ears flicked, his body lowered slightly, and his sharp gaze snapped upward.
Because at that moment—
Something was approaching.
From above.
Figures were flying in their direction.

chapters.title: Chapter 799: The Wrong Target
paragraphs: Through Pawpaw's eyes, Broken saw it clearly—five figures soaring through the sky, heading toward them.
Not toward him, but toward the group of players.
And those figures...
They were humanoid, but each had a pair of wings. Similar to Ivana.
The moment the players below noticed the approaching figures, their entire formation shifted. They grouped together, weapons ready, fully alert.
And Broken couldn't look away. Because those figures—he knew exactly what they were.
Then, the five winged beings landed.
The moment their feet touched the ground, moonlight revealed their forms.
They had dragon-like wings, scales covering parts of their arms and necks, and curved horns atop their heads.
There was no mistake.
Dragonkin.
The very ones they had been searching for... had finally revealed themselves.
"Dragonkin..." Broken whispered, relaying the information to SexyGrill.
Her head snapped toward him. "What? Really? Dragonkin?! How many?"
"Five."
As they watched, the players remained tense, their weapons still drawn, looking ready to react to anything the dragonkin might do.
Which raised an even bigger question—
Were these players really here to find the dragonkin?
Or had the dragonkin come to find them first?
Then, one of the players, a man who seemed to be their leader, took a step forward and spoke firmly to his companions. "Lower the weapons."
The tension in the air was undeniable as the players faced off against the five dragonkin.

Through Pawpaw's eyes, Broken could see everything—except their levels. His skill didn't let him analyze their strength, which meant if he wanted to gauge their power, he would have to see them with his own eyes.
One of the players, their leader, took a step forward and spoke in a calm but firm voice.
"We didn't come here to cause trouble."
So... their goal wasn't to hunt the dragonkin. But the fact that the leader immediately clarified this raised another question—had they met dragonkin before?
One of the dragonkin stepped forward, his scaly arms tense, his wings twitching slightly, his voice carrying an undeniable edge of anger.
"You players don't know your place. I know what you've done. You hurt our friend."
The players exchanged confused glances before the leader responded.

"What have we done? We've been exploring the forest and hunting monsters, that's all. We haven't harmed any of you. What 'friend' are you talking about? This is the first time we've even seen dragonkin."
The dragonkin's golden eyes narrowed as he spoke again, his voice filled with accusation.
"You hurt our friend. A wyvern."
A wyvern?
Broken's eyes sharpened as he processed those words.
A wyvern... could they mean the one he shot with an arrow before?
He frowned slightly. If that wyvern was connected to these dragonkin, then these five must have come here seeking revenge.
But the problem was—they had the wrong target. They thought these players were responsible.
"We saw wyverns roaming around this area several times... we never did anything to them," the player leader replied, his voice steady but wary.
But the dragonkin's expression hardened.
"Whether you did or not, we're going to make you leave this place."
The moment those words left his mouth, some of the players instinctively gripped their weapons, readying themselves for a fight.
However, the leader wasn't eager to engage.
"Hold." His voice was firm, demanding restraint from his group.
Yet, the dragonkin kept advancing toward them.
A ripple of panic spread through the players.
"They're going to kill us! We can't just stand here!"
"We can't even log out—we've already entered battle mode! This is bad!"
"Damn it, I don't want to have to start this whole damn trek over again!"
"We should defend ourselves!"
The leader's frustration was obvious, his voice rising. "Hold your ground! We didn't do anything they're accusing us of!"

From the way the players reacted, it was clear—they knew exactly how strong the dragonkin were. Even though their numbers outmatched the dragonkin 8-to-1, even though all of them were level 200 or higher, none of them were eager to fight.
Which raised a new question for Broken.
Just how powerful were these dragonkin?
Broken continued observing through Pawpaw's eyes, relaying everything he saw to SexyGrill.
"I'm sure a fight's going to break out," she said, her tone serious.
"Looks like it," Broken agreed.
"Should we step in?"
He paused, considering the situation carefully. "We came here to gather information from the dragonkin. If we interfere, we might end up making ourselves a threat to them."
"That makes sense," SexyGrill nodded. "Besides, we don't even know these players or why they're here."
Broken gave a small nod, agreeing with her reasoning.

To ensure he wouldn't lose track of the dragonkin, he deployed his flying golem. The mechanical construct immediately soared into the air, rising high above the treetops, ready to track their movements from above in case they decided to leave.
And just as they had predicted—it happened.
The dragonkin had no intention of listening to anything the players had to say.
Without warning, the first dragonkin shot forward with terrifying speed, slamming directly into one of the frontline players, sending him flying backward.
Broken swallowed hard, his heart pounding.
Just how powerful were these dragonkin?

The players reacted instantly. Buffs were cast, and they quickly shifted into a defensive formation—the frontliners bracing themselves to block the onslaught, while the ranged attackers unleashed spells and arrows from a distance.
Then—chaos erupted.
A massive explosion of skills, magic, and attacks filled the battlefield, as the players went all out, casting their strongest abilities with zero hesitation.
But...
What shocked Broken the most was that the dragonkin weren't fazed.
Not even a little.
They moved too fast, weaving through the attacks like unstoppable forces of destruction.
They tore through the players' defensive line, breaking formations, killing them with terrifying ease.
They were monsters.
Broken's eyes widened.
Their power was beyond anything he expected. If he had to guess... their levels had to be at least 250 or higher.
How else could they shrug off the attacks of forty players—all level 200+—without effort?
It was a one-sided massacre.
The entire battle lasted only a few minutes. And then—it was over.
The last surviving player barely had time to react before one of the dragonkin lunged forward, slashing his throat open with a single swipe of his claws.
Just like that.
Forty players—slaughtered effortlessly.
The dragonkin stood victorious, not a single one of them looking the least bit injured.
Broken could only stare.
These dragonkin weren't just strong.
They were absolute monsters.
If the players' group hadn't been so large, they might have been able to move unnoticed. But their numbers had made them an easy target, and now they had paid the price.
And the worst part?
They only became victims because of what Broken had done weeks ago—when he attacked that wyvern.
Now, with their hunt complete and every player slain, the five dragonkin stood amidst the carnage, their expressions unreadable.
One of the dragonkin scoffed. "They'll come back."
Another smirked. "Then we just have to kill every player we find. That's easy."
Their words were ice-cold—as if they truly didn't care about anything outside their own kind.
This wasn't just a hunt. This was their territory.
If five dragonkin were stationed here, there had to be more of them living deeper inside the region. This was their land, and they clearly did not welcome outsiders.
But just as they were about to turn and leave, one of them suddenly froze in place.
His head tilted slightly before his sharp golden eyes narrowed.
Then, he slowly turned around, scanning the area.
"...We're being watched."

SexyGrill leaned in slightly, whispering to him, "What's the plan, Broken?"
"We can't take the risk of revealing ourselves right now—not right after they just massacred an entire group of players in a blind rage," he murmured back.
"But if we don't try to talk to them now, they're going to leave," she countered.
"We can still follow them," Broken replied, his voice firm. "If we track them, we might be able to find their real base."
SexyGrill nodded slowly, understanding his reasoning.
Meanwhile, the dragonkin remained on high alert, their bodies tense, their movements calculated as if they were preparing to attack whoever they believed was spying on them.
But at the very least, Broken was sure Pawpaw wasn't the one who triggered their suspicion.
The demon cat stayed completely still, blending into the darkness, making no movements that could draw their attention.
Yet... the dragonkin's unease wasn't fading.
So who, or what, were they sensing?
These dragonkin... they were a real threat.
Broken knew he had to think carefully before making any move. Revealing himself now could be a mistake, especially when he still had no idea where they stood—were they allies or enemies?
More than that, he needed to understand their intentions before deciding anything.
Maylock had mentioned something before—a dragonkin had been seen in the High Elf Queen's palace in the Central Continent.
What did that mean?
Were these dragonkin opposed to the High Elves? Or were they working together?
Were they potential allies... or would they become an even bigger problem?
And then, there was Ivana.
If she had ever come to this place, shouldn't there be some kind of clue left behind? Something—anything—that indicated her presence?
Was she... possibly hiding among these dragonkin?
There were too many questions.
And Broken needed answers.
If he wanted to know where the dragonkin lived and where they were hiding, he had to track them first.
After watching for a while, Broken saw the dragonkin finally decide to leave. They walked a few steps before flapping their powerful wings and quickly taking off into the sky.
"Pawpaw, follow them from below. Stay hidden and don't get detected."
Without a sound, Pawpaw leapt from the tree, blending seamlessly into the shadows as he darted after the flying dragonkin.
But then—
One of the dragonkin suddenly stopped mid-air, hovering in place while the others turned to look at him.
What were they thinking?
At that exact moment, Broken realized the problem.
They weren't looking down.
They were looking up.
Right at Zepy, his flying golem.
"Zepy!"
In an instant, the dragonkin shot toward the golem, chasing it down at full speed!
"Zepy, hide! Get out of there!"
[Ethereal Cloak (Active Skill) activated]
The flying golem immediately vanished into invisibility, but the effect would only last for 10 seconds. And against enemies who could fly just as fast, hiding for only 10 seconds might not be enough.
Zepy bolted, flying away at max speed, but to Broken's horror, the dragonkin were still following.
They could still sense it.

Damn. These dragonkin were far more dangerous than he had expected. If they caught Zepy, they would destroy it instantly—and considering how much gold and rare materials he had spent to create the flying golem, that was absolutely not an option.
Thinking quickly, Broken made a decision.
He ordered Zepy to fly even further away, leading the dragonkin away from his real location.
Then—just before the invisibility wore off, Broken activated a skill.
[Summon Elemental Golem (Conditional Active Skill) Lv. 2 activated]
In an instant, Zepy disappeared from the air...
And reappeared right next to Broken.
He let out a deep breath, relief washing over him.
That was close. Too close.
His flying golem was priceless—recreating something this advanced wouldn't be easy. There was no way he was going to let it be destroyed.
SexyGrill let out a small laugh, clearly amused by how tense Broken had looked just moments ago, completely worried about Zepy's survival.
Broken turned to her, frowning slightly. "What? You have no idea how stressed I was. Do you know how much this golem cost me?"
She continued laughing. "Looks like we can't use the golem anymore. I'm sure the dragonkin will be way more alert now.
"Yeah... at least we still have Pawpaw." He let out a sigh, still recovering from the near loss of his flying creation.
Once he was certain the dragonkin had flown far enough away, Broken finally relaxed, leaning back against a tree with SexyGrill beside him.

Meanwhile, Pawpaw was still tracking them, running through the forest as fast as he could. Even if he couldn't match their speed, he kept following in their direction, hoping to find clues about their destination.
With no immediate threat nearby, Broken took a deep breath and made his next move.
He summoned Polly.
Without wasting time, the two of them climbed onto the bird-like mount. They had to be careful—using Blaze at night would be too risky, considering how bright and fiery the beast was.
This time, stealth was more important than power.

Broken and SexyGrill continued their journey through the night, constantly hounded by monsters from every direction. By now, they were used to this relentless jungle, where high-level creatures lurked everywhere, waiting for a chance to strike.
But despite the never-ending battles, Broken had to keep moving—he had to follow Pawpaw's direction and make the most of their time before he was forced to log out.
Then, after hours of non-stop combat, it finally happened.
Pawpaw signaled him.
And it came right after they had barely finished another fight.
Without hesitation, Broken activated his Shared Sense skill, shifting his vision to Pawpaw's perspective.
What he saw... was a location unlike anything they had encountered before.

Near the summit, a massive cliff rose high into the sky, towering above the dense forest below. From where Pawpaw stood, Broken could see strange openings along the rocky walls, leading somewhere deep inside.
The entire place looked like a fortress carved into the mountain itself.
Pawpaw crept closer, trying to get a better look.
But then—he suddenly froze.
Right as he stepped out into a clearing, the demon cat stopped dead in his tracks.
Broken frowned. "What's wrong, Pawpaw?"
He focused, observing through Pawpaw's eyes, and that was when he finally saw it.
A transparent layer covered the entire massive area, stretching across the cliffside and everything within it.
A domain.
The entire place was protected by a powerful barrier.
Broken immediately ordered Pawpaw to retreat, not wanting to risk the dragonkin detecting him.
This place was clearly hidden for a reason.
If they had gone through the trouble of shielding it with a domain, then there was definitely something important inside.
Broken took a deep breath, his mind racing with possibilities.
Then, he turned to SexyGrill and spoke with certainty.
"We've finally found our destination."
